item.title: WWE star Ludwig Kaiser’s battery case dismissal motion denied
item.description: WWE star Ludwig Kaiser’s battery case dismissal motion denied appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Earlier this year, WWE Superstar Ludwig Kaiser, aka Marcel Barthel, was arrested in Florida . Kaiser, currently performing as El Grande Americano in WWE’s Mexican wrestling promotion AAA, was arrested on battery charges in Orange County, Florida. As per reports, Barthel was arrested on May 20, 2026, on charges of battery in Orange County, Florida. According to the online records, he was booked in Orange County, Florida, at 2:37 PM. Later, PWInsider confirmed through their report that Barthel was bonded out of Orange County Corrections on a $1000 bail by his WWE colleague and close friend, Gunther. Now, following a court hearing on Monday, Oct. 19, 2026, a motion filed by Kaiser to dismiss his battery case was denied. Kaiser’s legal team aimed to have the misdemeanor battery charge dropped by invoking Florida’s “Stand Your Ground” law. The claim was that Kaiser was justified in applying the level of force he did against the alleged victim because he reasonably believed it was needed to defend himself and his girlfriend, Andre Bazarte, from the “imminent use of unlawful force.” A pre-trial conference is scheduled to take place on Dec. 17, 2026. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) More on WWE Superstar Ludwig Kaiser’s charges Earlier this year, Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful and trusted media personality Raj Giri had opened up and shared details about Kaiser’s arrest and charges. Previously, the charges were suspected to be domestic charges, but they were later dismissed by Sean Ross Sapp. “This is what I heard regarding the Ludwig Kaiser situation. He was in the apartment elevator with Andrea Bazarte and they were being affectionate, but nothing crazy or out of the ordinary. [Richard] Reap allegedly didn’t say anything in the elevator but once he got out on the 12th floor, he allegedly said something to Kaiser to the effect of ‘you need to show some f’n respect before I call ICE on that b**ch.’ Kaiser got out of the elevator and they had a little scuffle, but no punches were apparently thrown,” Giri wrote. Related: WWE’s R-Truth breaks silence after match was stopped after he ‘almost passed away’ Related: WWE star Stephanie Vaquer breaks the internet with Hawaii thirst traps

item.title: ‘There’s a Reason He Lives in Denver’ — Radio Host Makes Pointed Observation About Peyton Manning Potentially Buying a Stake in the Colts
item.description: ‘There’s a Reason He Lives in Denver’ — Radio Host Makes Pointed Observation About Peyton Manning Potentially Buying a Stake in the Colts The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday. Before the day was out, a report linked Peyton Manning to both the job and a stake in the team. However, Indianapolis radio host Jake Query of “1075 The Fan” sees two big problems with bringing Manning back. Why Jake Query Doubts a Peyton Manning-Colts Homecoming Late Jim Irsay’s three daughters now own the Colts, with Carlie Irsay-Gordon serving as principal owner and CEO. Query’s math assumes Manning would pay full value to join them. “Peyton Manning’s net worth is approximated to be around $300 million… $300 million dollars would buy Peyton Manning roughly four percent of what the team is worth,” Query said. The math just about checks out. Using a roughly $8 billion franchise valuation, $300 million would equal only about 4% of the team’s headline value, before accounting for liquidity, transaction terms, or any minority-stake discount. Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio pointed out that NFL rules would prevent the Colts from giving Manning equity as compensation for serving as GM, though he could separately buy an ownership stake. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Query’s second problem has nothing to do with money: “It is my belief, not fact, that Peyton Manning, as much as he has a reverence for Indianapolis, and as much as he is now a beloved adopted son of Indianapolis, Peyton Manning will never, and I’m not saying he should get over the fact that he was cut by the Indianapolis Colts.” As evidence, Query pointed to where Manning, who retired a decade ago, now spends his time: “There’s a reason he lives in Denver… there’s a reason why he’s at Nuggets games and Broncos games.” The report came from Dan Patrick, who passed along what a source had told him on “The Dan Patrick Show”: “The Colts’ first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning.” The call, Patrick added , “will explore whether or not Peyton would be interested in being a General Manager of the Colts as an entry point that would include ownership interest in the Colts.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Mike Chappell of Fox59/CBS4 has since reported that the Colts have not yet reached out to Manning, though he noted that doesn’t mean they won’t. Patrick also raised a possible snag, adding: “Now my source says the only question will be Peyton’s family. They enjoyed Denver quite a bit.” Denver is also where Manning’s name came up in ownership talk before. When the Denver Broncos were up for sale in 2021, Jason La Canfora, then with CBS Sports, reported that Manning had held talks with several ownership groups seen as favorites to buy the team. item.content:encoded: ‘There’s a Reason He Lives in Denver’ — Radio Host Makes Pointed Observation About Peyton Manning Potentially Buying a Stake in the Colts The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday. Before the day was out, a report linked Peyton Manning to both the job and a stake in the team. However, Indianapolis radio host Jake Query of “1075 The Fan” sees two big problems with bringing Manning back. Why Jake Query Doubts a Peyton Manning-Colts Homecoming Late Jim Irsay’s three daughters now own the Colts, with Carlie Irsay-Gordon serving as principal owner and CEO. Query’s math assumes Manning would pay full value to join them. “Peyton Manning’s net worth is approximated to be around $300 million… $300 million dollars would buy Peyton Manning roughly four percent of what the team is worth,” Query said. The math just about checks out. Using a roughly $8 billion franchise valuation, $300 million would equal only about 4% of the team’s headline value, before accounting for liquidity, transaction terms, or any minority-stake discount. Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio pointed out that NFL rules would prevent the Colts from giving Manning equity as compensation for serving as GM, though he could separately buy an ownership stake. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Query’s second problem has nothing to do with money: “It is my belief, not fact, that Peyton Manning, as much as he has a reverence for Indianapolis, and as much as he is now a beloved adopted son of Indianapolis, Peyton Manning will never, and I’m not saying he should get over the fact that he was cut by the Indianapolis Colts.” As evidence, Query pointed to where Manning, who retired a decade ago, now spends his time: “There’s a reason he lives in Denver… there’s a reason why he’s at Nuggets games and Broncos games.” The report came from Dan Patrick, who passed along what a source had told him on “The Dan Patrick Show”: “The Colts’ first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning.” The call, Patrick added , “will explore whether or not Peyton would be interested in being a General Manager of the Colts as an entry point that would include ownership interest in the Colts.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Mike Chappell of Fox59/CBS4 has since reported that the Colts have not yet reached out to Manning, though he noted that doesn’t mean they won’t. Patrick also raised a possible snag, adding: “Now my source says the only question will be Peyton’s family. They enjoyed Denver quite a bit.” Denver is also where Manning’s name came up in ownership talk before. When the Denver Broncos were up for sale in 2021, Jason La Canfora, then with CBS Sports, reported that Manning had held talks with several ownership groups seen as favorites to buy the team. No formal role came of it once the group led by Rob Walton came out on top. Manning has turned down a high-profile pitch before. ESPN repeatedly pursued Manning for the “Monday Night Football” booth after his retirement, including sending executives to Denver, but he declined. A full-time GM role could also complicate Manning’s media commitments. Florio argued it would likely mean giving up ManningCast and potentially stepping back from Omaha Productions. Florio noted in his column that “while it makes plenty of sense for the Colts to want him now, if Manning wanted to live that life he probably already would be.” Meanwhile, Ballard’s tenure, in its 10th season, ended one day after the previously winless Tennessee Titans came back from a 13-0 halftime deficit to beat the Colts 26-20 at Lucas Oil Stadium. The loss dropped the Colts to 2-4, though they sit second in the AFC South. They play the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday, October 25, in Week 7. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Barcelona forced to wear last season’s orange kit for Champions League clash vs PSG
item.description: Barcelona forced to wear last season’s orange kit for Champions League clash vs PSG FC Barcelona will lock horns with Paris Saint-Germain later tonight in an eagerly-awaited UEFA Champions League clash away at Parc des Princes. And, as reported by Tot Costa (h/t SPORT ), Barcelona will have to bring back last season’s orange kit for their Champions League visit to PSG after UEFA ruled that none of their three current kits could be used for the match. As per the report, the decision has been driven by television broadcast requirements, with UEFA seeking to ensure a clear visual distinction between the two teams. None of this season’s kits can be used Barcelona will wear orange against PSG. The choice has also appeared in the club’s official promotional material for the match, featuring Lamine Yamal, Pedri and Anthony Gordon wearing last season’s shirt. The decision comes despite Barça training on Monday in their blue training kit, which had suggested that they might use their third strip, designed in two shades of electric blue. However, neither their traditional blaugrana shirt, their black-and-purple second kit dedicated to Kobe Bryant, nor their blue alternative has been approved for the fixture. All three have been ruled out on television broadcast grounds, forcing the La Liga champions to look beyond their current collection. Last season’s Nike Total 90 shirt returns The orange shirt comes from Nike’s Total 90 collection, inspired by football fashion in the early 2000s. Barcelona have already worn it during pre-season, including in a friendly against Basel, but will now bring it back for a competitive match of major importance. Barcelona wore last season’s orange kit in a friendly vs Basel. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) The situation highlights an unusual problem for a club with three kits available for the current season: being unable to use any of them for a particular fixture. The colour combinations of PSG’s kit and the requirements of the television broadcast have left Barcelona without an approved option from their current range. As a result, Flick’s side must adjust their plans and revive last season’s orange strip for their meeting with PSG at the Parc des Princes, aiming to extend their winning start to the season to 12 games.

item.title: How and where to watch Como 1907 vs Manchester United across the globe
item.description: How and where to watch Como 1907 vs Manchester United across the globe Manchester United travel to Italy to face Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night. With just two wins in ten matches, the Red Devils are desperate for three points, especially after losing last time out against Atletico Madrid in the competition. Europe The match is scheduled during the earlier slot of European fixtures, as it starts at 17:45 local time in the UK and Ireland. TNT Sports holds the rights to broadcast the game in both countries. In Portugal, the match will kick off at the same time but will be broadcast on DAZN. Supporters in Spain can catch the game on Movistar, with the match starting at 18:45 local time. French viewers can tune in on Canal Plus, and German fans can watch on DAZN. North America The match will be shown on Paramount+ in the United States, with kick-off at 13:45 Eastern Time, 12:45 Central, 11:45 Mountain, and 10:45 on the west coast. In Canada, fans can tune in on DAZN. Africa Moroccan supporters can watch the game at 16:45 local time on beIN Sports. Cameroonian and Nigerian fans can see the match from 17:45 on SuperSport, while South African fans can watch at 18:45. Kenyans will have to wait a little longer, until 19:45, to see the match. Asia Chinese fans can tune in on iQiyi from 00:45 on Thursday morning, while Japanese supporters will have to stay up until 01:45 to watch the game on WOWOW. Finally, Australians will be able to catch the game at 03:45 early on Thursday morning on Stan Sport. Featured image by Michael Steele via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Copa Sudamericana 2026 Semi-Finals Preview: Brazilian Sides Hold Advantage Ahead Of 2nd Legs
item.description: Copa Sudamericana 2026 Semi-Finals Preview: Brazilian Sides Hold Advantage Ahead Of 2nd Legs By Louis Smith. The 2026 Copa Sudamericana final is almost set in stone. We head into the semi-final stage with four teams: Vasco da Gama, Atlético Mineiro, Montevideo City Torque and Boca Juniors, all gunning for a place in the final. Vasco da Gama v Boca Juniors We start with Vasco and Argentinian side Boca, where Vasco enjoyed a 1-0 victory in Argentina, giving them a huge advantage heading into the home leg. It was a great cross by Andrés Gómez, who has been one of Vasco’s best players this season, which met the head of Adson, who headed past his fellow countryman Álvaro Montero to give Vasco an important 1-0 victory. However, the disappointing thing for Vasco is that Gómez was later sent off after receiving two yellow cards, meaning they will be without a key asset for such a huge fixture. Vasco’s last major trophy came in 2011, when they lifted the Copa do Brasil, and they haven’t won a continental trophy since 1998, when they lifted the Copa Libertadores . Their last major final, excluding state championships, came last season in 2025, when they suffered a 2-1 defeat to Corinthians in the Copa do Brasil. They will be licking their lips at the prospect of booking their place in next month’s final. For Boca, their last continental triumph came back in 2007, when they lifted the Libertadores. They have also tasted success in the Copa Sudamericana , winning the competition on two occasions, in 2004 and 2005. However, since then, they have lost three Libertadores finals, including defeats to rivals River Plate in 2018 and, more recently, Fluminense in Rio de Janeiro after extra time in 2023. Atlético Mineiro v Montevideo City Torque Last season’s beaten finalists Atlético Mineiro enjoyed a fantastic 3-0 victory over Montevideo City Torque last week. Some patient play from Galo saw them take a 1-0 lead through Reinier before a lovely run, dribble and finish from Bernard saw them race into a 2-0 lead. Then, to put the cherry on the cake, a lovely ground pass from Renan Lodi set up Thiago Borbas, who has been in good form in recent weeks, to make it 3-0. Galo have not won a major continental title since lifting the Copa Libertadores in 2013 and have had rotten luck in recent finals. In 2024, they suffered a 3-1 defeat to Botafogo despite playing the majority of the match with a man advantage. Then, in 2025, they reached the Copa Sudamericana final , where they suffered penalty shootout heartbreak against Lanús in Asunción. It’s also worth noting that in 2024, they suffered defeat in the Copa do Brasil final. Their opponents, Montevideo City Torque, have never featured in a continental final, having only been formed 18 years ago and since been taken over by the City Football Group. It’s going to be a difficult task for them to overturn a three-goal deficit. However, they can still see this season as a success, considering their small stature and relatively short history. Despite the recent purple patch of the Uruguayan national team and the country’s continued production of talent, no Uruguayan club has reached a continental final since Peñarol did so in the Copa Libertadores in 2011. It’s also worth noting that no Uruguayan side has ever reached a Copa Sudamericana final, so if Montevideo City Torque are to progress, they would become the first club from the country to do so.

item.title: This day in Juventus history: Ten minutes of fury against Napoli signal the real dawn of a dynasty
item.description: TURIN, ITALY - OCTOBER 20: Martin Caceres of FC Juventus #4 scores the first goal during the Serie A match between FC Juventus and SSC Napoli at Juventus Arena on October 20, 2012 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) | Getty Images On October 20, 2012, Juventus Stadium hosted a clash that felt less like a mid-autumn league fixture and more like an early referendum on Italian football dominance. Antonio Conte’s side entered Matchday 8 attempting to prove that their unbeaten, surprise 2011–12 Scudetto was no mere flash in the pan. Standing directly across from them was Walter Mazzarri’s ferocious Napoli. Both sides arrived in Turin level at the top of the table, each boasting identical records of six wins and a draw from their opening seven fixtures. Juventus lined up in what would soon become the unmistakable blueprint of their era-defining dominance. With Marco Storari stepping into goal for an injured Gianluigi Buffon, the backline was anchored by the legendary ‘BBC’ trio — Andrea Barzagli, Leonardo Bonucci, and Giorgio Chiellini. Stephan Lichtsteiner and Kwadwo Asamoah patrolled the flanks, while the formidable midfield of Arturo Vidal, Andrea Pirlo, and Claudio Marchisio pulled the strings. Up front, Sebastian Giovinco and Fabio Quagliarella led the line in Conte’s signature 3-5-2. While the final scoreline suggested a comfortable afternoon for the hosts, the match sat on a razor’s edge for 80 excruciating minutes. Early on, Napoli nearly landed a knockout blow. In the 26th minute, Edinson Cavani whipped a vicious free kick from the edge of the penalty area that beat Storari clean, only to crash off the corner of the woodwork. Beyond that moment of heart-in-mouth drama, the first half degenerated into an intense tactical chess match, with both sides combining for just six total shot attempts and a single shot inside either box. The second half brought far more urgency. Just three minutes after the restart, Pirlo began testing Napoli’s resolve, forcing a sharp save from another trademark free kick. Seven minutes later, Asamoah found Giovinco inside the box with room to turn, but the Formica Atomica dragged his effort inches wide of the far post. In the 65th minute, Pirlo floated a stunning, pinpoint long ball over the top to sub Alessandro Matri, who tantalizingly failed to cushion the drop in what would have been a clear 1-v-1 with the keeper. As time ticked away, the match begged for a moment of raw inspiration. It arrived in the 80th minute. Earning a corner on the left, Pirlo curled a perfectly placed delivery directly into the heart of the six-yard box. Substitute Martín Cáceres timed his run to perfection, rising above a crowded penalty area to thunder a header past Morgan De Sanctis and shatter the deadlock. item.content:encoded: TURIN, ITALY - OCTOBER 20: Martin Caceres of FC Juventus #4 scores the first goal during the Serie A match between FC Juventus and SSC Napoli at Juventus Arena on October 20, 2012 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) | Getty Images On October 20, 2012, Juventus Stadium hosted a clash that felt less like a mid-autumn league fixture and more like an early referendum on Italian football dominance. Antonio Conte’s side entered Matchday 8 attempting to prove that their unbeaten, surprise 2011–12 Scudetto was no mere flash in the pan. Standing directly across from them was Walter Mazzarri’s ferocious Napoli. Both sides arrived in Turin level at the top of the table, each boasting identical records of six wins and a draw from their opening seven fixtures. Juventus lined up in what would soon become the unmistakable blueprint of their era-defining dominance. With Marco Storari stepping into goal for an injured Gianluigi Buffon, the backline was anchored by the legendary ‘BBC’ trio — Andrea Barzagli, Leonardo Bonucci, and Giorgio Chiellini. Stephan Lichtsteiner and Kwadwo Asamoah patrolled the flanks, while the formidable midfield of Arturo Vidal, Andrea Pirlo, and Claudio Marchisio pulled the strings. Up front, Sebastian Giovinco and Fabio Quagliarella led the line in Conte’s signature 3-5-2. While the final scoreline suggested a comfortable afternoon for the hosts, the match sat on a razor’s edge for 80 excruciating minutes. Early on, Napoli nearly landed a knockout blow. In the 26th minute, Edinson Cavani whipped a vicious free kick from the edge of the penalty area that beat Storari clean, only to crash off the corner of the woodwork. Beyond that moment of heart-in-mouth drama, the first half degenerated into an intense tactical chess match, with both sides combining for just six total shot attempts and a single shot inside either box. The second half brought far more urgency. Just three minutes after the restart, Pirlo began testing Napoli’s resolve, forcing a sharp save from another trademark free kick. Seven minutes later, Asamoah found Giovinco inside the box with room to turn, but the Formica Atomica dragged his effort inches wide of the far post. In the 65th minute, Pirlo floated a stunning, pinpoint long ball over the top to sub Alessandro Matri, who tantalizingly failed to cushion the drop in what would have been a clear 1-v-1 with the keeper. As time ticked away, the match begged for a moment of raw inspiration. It arrived in the 80th minute. Earning a corner on the left, Pirlo curled a perfectly placed delivery directly into the heart of the six-yard box. Substitute Martín Cáceres timed his run to perfection, rising above a crowded penalty area to thunder a header past Morgan De Sanctis and shatter the deadlock. Before Napoli could even process the blow, Juventus delivered the lethal knockout. Just two minutes later, a blocked Giovinco shot spilled out toward the edge of the area. A 19-year-old Paul Pogba — having come off the bench just moments earlier — tracked the high bounce and struck a pristine, chest-high volley through a sea of bodies, beating De Sanctis at the near post to send Juventus Stadium into delirium. In the end, two sides sitting atop the table — who would ultimately finish first and second at the season’s conclusion — fought to an absolute standstill for eighty minutes. But champions are defined by how they command the margin between parity and victory. In those final ten minutes, Juventus didn’t just win a high-stakes fixture. They asserted their dominance, bent their primary rival to their will, and laid the permanent foundation for a nine-year empire.

item.title: Shohei Ohtani Dodgers jersey from Tokyo Series makes history
item.description: The legend of Shohei Ohtani continues to grow. The jersey that the Los Angeles Dodgers superstar wore in the opening game of the 2025 Tokyo Series broke the record for most expensive jersey worn by a baseball player in the 21st century. The jersey sold for $2,055,700 in an auction from The Realest , the company said in a press release on Monday, Oct. 19. The uniform featured the first gold MLB logo in the league's history. Ohtani was one of six players in 2025 to wear the Logoman patch, which was given to the winners of the previous campaign's major awards. He won the 2024 National League MVP after becoming the first player in MLB history to hit 50 home runs and steal 50 bases in a season . Several of the patches were removed and turned into trading cards, so it is unique that this one remains intact. The jersey, which was certified by The Realest's authentication program, also has a Tokyo Series patch and the Fernando Valenzuela patch the Dodgers wore that season after they won the 2024 World Series. It was autographed by the MLB superstar in kanji characters to further celebrate his heritage and the culture of the city the 2025 season opener was played in. It was Ohtani's first Major League Baseball game in his home country. He went 2-for-5 with a double in the Dodgers' 4-1 win over the Chicago Cubs at the Tokyo Dome. “The greatest collectibles are the ones that capture moments that can never be recreated, and this jersey represents exactly that,” Scott Keeney, also known as DJ Skee, who is the founder and CEO of The Realest, said in a statement. “Ohtani is redefining what’s possible in the collectibles market, and the global response to this jersey reinforces just how significant these historic artifacts have become." The Realest put the Ohtani jersey on display at ComplexCon in Los Angeles earlier this month alongside the last No. 8 jersey that Kobe Bryant wore in the NBA Finals. The company said that the winner of the auction also received the custom shrine featuring Japanese motifs that the jersey was displayed in. The previous record for most expensive baseball jersey worn in this century was held by a New York Yankees jersey that Aaron Judge wore in his MLB debut in 2016 when he hit a home run in his first at-bat. That jersey sold for a reported $1.792 million. It last went to auction in July at Sotheby's alongside Derek Jeter's game-worn jersey from "The Dive." Earlier this year, Ohtani's game-worn and autographed New Balance cleats from the same Tokyo Series game were sold by The Realest for $440,055, making them the highest-selling baseball cleat ever. This number puts the shoes in the same conversation as sneakers worn by Michael Jordan . Ohtani was the MLB Rookie of the Year in 2018 after he debuted with the Los Angeles Angels. item.title: Green Bay Packers add former first-round pick amid defensive line injury concerns
item.description: The Green Bay Packers are searching for defensive line help after injuries weakened their options up front. With starting nose tackle Javon Hargrave out, veteran Chris McClellan is expected to fill the role, but Green Bay has limited depth behind him. To strengthen the rotation, the Packers have signed a former first round pick to their practice squad. ESPN reporters Adam Schefter and Rob Demovsky announced on X, (formerly Twitter), that Green Bay has added defensive tackle Mazi Smith to its practice squad. Mazi Smith entered the NFL as a first-round selection by Dallas in 2023 after playing college football at Michigan. He spent two and a half seasons with the Cowboys before moving to the New York Jets last fall in the trade involving Quinnen Williams. Mazi Smith’s fit with the Green Bay Packers Oct 6, 2024; Inglewood, California, USA; The Green Bay Packers defense celebrates after safety Xavier McKinney (29) intercepted a Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (not pictured) pass in the third quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Hanashiro-Imagn Images Smith finished the 2025 season with New York and also appeared for the Jets during the preseason before joining the Miami Dolphins. He now heads to Green Bay, where he will look to earn a place in the Packers’ defensive line rotation. The 25-year-old saw regular action as part of Dallas’ defensive line rotation during his first two NFL seasons. His most productive year came in 2024, when he appeared in all 17 games and recorded 41 tackles and one sack. His role shrank considerably last fall, as he managed just three tackles across five appearances. Jan 10, 2026; Chicago, IL, USA; in Green Bay Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon (25) runs with the ball against the Chicago Bears an NFC Wild Card Round game at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Smith lost his place in the Cowboys’ defensive line rotation before Dallas traded him to New York. After stints with both the Jets and Dolphins, he now has another chance to earn playing time in Green Bay. With Javon Hargrave and other key defensive linemen sidelined, the Packers need reinforcements up front. Smith’s ability to take advantage of the opportunity could play a major role in determining his future in the NFL. India lead the overall T20I head-to-head against New Zealand 17-11 from 31 completed matches, with three ties. India have won six of the nine bilateral T20I series between the two sides, including four of the five played in India. India's T20I record in New Zealand ahead of the October 22 series opener India begin a record 12-match tour of New Zealand on Thursday, October 22, with the first of five T20Is at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. New Zealand Cricket announced the schedule in June, and the tour also includes five ODIs and two Tests before it ends on December 1. The T20I leg comes more than seven months after India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the T20 World Cup final in Ahmedabad. India had also won a bilateral T20I series 4-1 at home in January, which gives them the better recent record against this opponent. New Zealand has been a tougher place for India to win, though. India have played four T20I series there and won two, losing the other two by 2-0 in 2008/09 and 2-1 in 2018/19. The record below covers home and away matches and every series played. India lead the overall T20I head-to-head 17-11 from 31 completed matches, with three ties. New Zealand won both neutral-venue meetings, at the 2007 T20 World Cup in Johannesburg and the 2021 edition in Dubai, while two other games, in 2012 and 2022, had no result. item.title: What Gary Player once said about LIV golfers attempting to play on the PGA Tour
item.description: Photo by Andrew Redington/Getty Images LIV Golf is bankrupt, and rather than sticking around for LIV 2.0 for far less money, players are jumping ship. Golfers were expected to leave the tour this fall because of growing uncertainty about LIV’s future, but how many was unknown. The reality has been a worst-case scenario for the breakaway golf league. Jon Rahm left, which was expected. The three-time individual champion has been set on returning to the DP World Tour for months. But with him went Joaquin Niemann and Sergio Garcia, and even Cameron Smith is weighing his options. The PGA Tour and the DP World Tour now face the conundrum of what to do with these players. DP World Tour players are already expressing frustration that these players are returning to the tour unpunished, taking spots from other members. When LIV Golf was first created, Gary Player shared his honest thoughts on what the future holds for these players. Gary Player said LIV golfers ‘can’t have your cake and eat it’ When LIV Golf launched in 2022, Player was mostly supportive of players signing for eye-watering sums of money. He said people have the right to put their families first, but he also admitted these players couldn’t have it both ways. Speaking to Sky Sports News, Player said, “Remember this, the players who are playing there now, they need the money. They’ve got families and I don’t blame them for playing there. There’s not a lot of them who can win on the regular tour anymore, so they are wisely taking the money.” “There is a place in the sun for both tours. I just hope they settle everything in an amicable way and we go from strength to strength because golf is a passport to the world.” But when asked if he believed players should be allowed to play on the PGA Tour, the nine-time major winner responded, “If they so desire to play the LIV tour which is their choice and their freedom… freedom is on the wane around the world, so they still have their freedom to choose and we should be grateful for that. “But…you can’t have both tours, you can’t do that, it’s not going to be allowed according to the rules, as far as I know.” “I’d like the people that are playing this tour just to be open and say, ‘Look, I’m playing here because I want to make some money, I have a family’. There’s no disgrace in that. But you can’t have your cake and eat it.” As players leave LIV Golf, the PGA Tour has stood firm. CEO Brian Rolapp said no discussions are underway to allow players like Rahm to negotiate their way back. They’ll all have to serve their one-year suspension, spending a year on the DP World Tour. And gradually, more and more players are admitting they moved for the money. Graeme McDowell said he wished he had said that all along. Four years later, and Player’s initial opinion on LIV Golf has aged exceptionally well. Speaking to Sky Sports News, Player said, “Remember this, the players who are playing there now, they need the money. They’ve got families and I don’t blame them for playing there. There’s not a lot of them who can win on the regular tour anymore, so they are wisely taking the money.” “There is a place in the sun for both tours. I just hope they settle everything in an amicable way and we go from strength to strength because golf is a passport to the world.” But when asked if he believed players should be allowed to play on the PGA Tour, the nine-time major winner responded, “If they so desire to play the LIV tour which is their choice and their freedom… freedom is on the wane around the world, so they still have their freedom to choose and we should be grateful for that. “But…you can’t have both tours, you can’t do that, it’s not going to be allowed according to the rules, as far as I know.” “I’d like the people that are playing this tour just to be open and say, ‘Look, I’m playing here because I want to make some money, I have a family’. There’s no disgrace in that. But you can’t have your cake and eat it.” As players leave LIV Golf, the PGA Tour has stood firm. CEO Brian Rolapp said no discussions are underway to allow players like Rahm to negotiate their way back. They’ll all have to serve their one-year suspension, spending a year on the DP World Tour. And gradually, more and more players are admitting they moved for the money. Graeme McDowell said he wished he had said that all along. Four years later, and Player’s initial opinion on LIV Golf has aged exceptionally well. item.title: Today on Pinstripe Alley – 10/20/26
item.description: Oct 19, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; The Tampa Bay Rays celebrate defeating the Cleveland Guardians in game six of the ALCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a long October’s journey into, well, still October, we have our World Series matchup. It’ll be Rays vs. Brewers, Tampa Bay dispatching the Guardians with relative ease last night to win the third pennant in franchise history. As shocking as it may seem on the surface, with each side playing for its first ever title, in the context of this season it’s really only a total surprise to those who weren’t paying much attention all along. The Rays and Brewers paced their respective leagues for almost the entire year, earned number-one seeds at the end of the regular season, and now will deservedly play for the championship. On the site this morning, Madison will recap what went down in Game 6 last night. Also, Josh keeps our report card series going with a review of Paul Blackburn’s wonderful 2026 campaign, and Andrés writes up the one and only Mickey Mantle, precisely 95 years after the day of Mantle’s birth. And later, John discusses his experience attending 20 Yankees home games this year. Today’s Playoff Matchup: Offday. Questions/Prompts: 1. If you can hold to the side your particular like (or dislike) for either team, how excited are you for a Brewers/Rays World Series just on the basis of the quality of the teams, and their styles of play? 2. What was the best (define best however you want) series of the playoffs to this point?

item.title: MM 10.20: Maryland tennis’ Anastasiia Sorska earns spot in NCAA fall singles championship
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - JULY 01: Anastasiia Sorska of Ukraine and Mailuodi Lei of China celebrate a point in the Girls Doubles during the Lexus British Open Roehampton at Wimbledon Qualifying and Community Sports Centre on July 01, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Patrick Khachfe/Getty Images for LTA) | Getty Images for LTA Multiple Maryland tennis players have continued to ride their momentum this fall season, and Anastasiia Sorska is no exception. The freshman became the first Terp since 2021 to make the NCAA fall singles championship after going undefeated at ITA Atlantic regionals. FRESHMAN PHENOM🐢 For the first time since 2021, the Terps will have an NCAA Singles Fall Championship representative!🙌 Nastya punches her ticket to compete after reaching the semifinals at the ITA Atlantic Regionals!🎾🎟️ pic.twitter.com/VcweS42sHt — Maryland Tennis (@TerpTennis) October 19, 2026 Sorska ultimately punched her ticket to the national tournament after defeating Virginia’s Vivian Yang in two sets on Monday. She has not lost a set all tournament and is one of the highest-touted recruits by the Terps in years.. She wasn’t the only Maryland standout during Monday’s draw, however. Emma Ghirardato and Diya Challa claimed victory in their semifinal matchup and will have a chance to qualify for the NCAA fall doubles championship Tuesday. In other news Maryland women’s basketball took down Virginia Tech, 93-82, in its first exhibition game. Chase Cook had the game story . Maryland men’s basketball jumped up in Jon Rothstein’s preseason power rankings. Maryland is up to No. 34 in @JonRothstein ’s Preseason Top-45 Power Rankings 🐢 pic.twitter.com/FvDsf2aAVt — Inside Maryland Sports (@Terrapins247) October 19, 2026 Maryland football four-star defensive back commit Kenaz Sullivan visited Virginia Tech. Go Hokies??🟠🦃 pic.twitter.com/885AZ9SsBX — naz-island 4⭐️ (@KenazSullivan) October 20, 2026 The Terps also released their game time for their home matchup against Illinois on Halloween. Halloween at The Shell 🎃🐢 📰 https://t.co/URhinlqXtF pic.twitter.com/tOPo7jppEs — Maryland Football (@TerpsFootball) October 19, 2026

item.title: Phillies Eye Future Star Shortstop Free Agent After Trea Turner Update
item.description: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - AUGUST 31: Trea Turner #7 of the Philadelphia Phillies stands in the dugout before the MLB game against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on August 31, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies have several important decisions to make this offseason after another postseason disappointment, and few will draw more attention than the uncertainty at shortstop. Franchise shortstop Trea Turner remains a necessary part of the club’s plans going into the fifth season of his 11-year, $300 million contract , but president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski has made clear that he must improve defensively to keep the position in 2027. Turner endured a brutal season at the plate and on defense and shortly afterward, Dombrowski announced that a position change could be considered if Turner cannot return to a reliable level of defense. “Turner, 33, had perhaps the worst season of his career — hitting .242 with a .675 OPS with a league-worst 21 errors at shortstop — and Dombrowski warned (last week) that a position change could be on deck if Turner fails to regain his form as even an average fielding shortstop,” the Associated Press reported . That uncertainty could open the door for Philadelphia to explore alternatives for the roster, including a highly regarded international shortstop drawing attention from several major league organizations. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets Outfielder Cuts Ties With Team Immediately After Season Ends Philadelphia Phillies Circling Young Infield Star As the team considers its possible alternatives at shortstop, a South Korean report has surfaced indicating that the team has its eyes on a pending international free agent star. “Kim Joo-won’s performance has been steadily improving every year, and Major League Baseball is consistently keeping an eye on him,” according to a translated report from Korean outlet OSEN . “At least four to five teams, including the New York Mets, Philadelphia Phillies, and Pittsburgh Pirates, visit Changwon NC Park to continuously observe Kim Joo-won.” Kim has built a reputation as a key shortstop for South Korea’s national team and in the Korean Baseball Organization (KBO) league. “The day is not far off when ‘national team shortstop’ Kim Joo-won will be called a big league shortstop,” OSEN added. “Players can explore overseas opportunities via the posting system after their seventh season; based on the (free agent) registration requirement of 145 days per season, Kim Joo-won has completed a total of five seasons up to this year…” As a result, Kim wouldn’t be an option to replace Turner next season, but he could factor into the Phillies’ future plans depending on how the infield mix develops. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies have several important decisions to make this offseason after another postseason disappointment, and few will draw more attention than the uncertainty at shortstop. Franchise shortstop Trea Turner remains a necessary part of the club’s plans going into the fifth season of his 11-year, $300 million contract , but president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski has made clear that he must improve defensively to keep the position in 2027. That uncertainty could open the door for Philadelphia to explore alternatives for the roster, including a highly regarded international shortstop drawing attention from several major league organizations. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets Outfielder Cuts Ties With Team Immediately After Season Ends Philadelphia Phillies Circling Young Infield Star As the team considers its possible alternatives at shortstop, a South Korean report has surfaced indicating that the team has its eyes on a pending international free agent star. “Kim Joo-won’s performance has been steadily improving every year, and Major League Baseball is consistently keeping an eye on him,” according to a translated report from Korean outlet OSEN . “At least four to five teams, including the New York Mets, Philadelphia Phillies, and Pittsburgh Pirates, visit Changwon NC Park to continuously observe Kim Joo-won.” Kim has built a reputation as a key shortstop for South Korea’s national team and in the Korean Baseball Organization (KBO) league. “The day is not far off when ‘national team shortstop’ Kim Joo-won will be called a big league shortstop,” OSEN added. “Players can explore overseas opportunities via the posting system after their seventh season; based on the (free agent) registration requirement of 145 days per season, Kim Joo-won has completed a total of five seasons up to this year…” As a result, Kim wouldn’t be an option to replace Turner next season, but he could factor into the Phillies’ future plans depending on how the infield mix develops. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Trump’s Yankees Ally Going Nowhere After ‘Total Fake News’ Dismissal Update, Per Insider Trea Turner’s Defense Puts Philadelphia Phillies Shortstop Plans In Focus Turner’s status makes the position worth watching as the Phillies reshape their coaching staff and roster. Dombrowski has emphasized that Turner can remain the starting shortstop if he recovers the defensive form he showed previously, but it seems like just a matter of time before the Phillies will need an alternative on the roster. Kim’s reported presence on Philadelphia’s scouting radar adds another name to the broader conversation. It also marks an intriguing foray into international scouting for a Phillies franchise that has not traditionally targeted major overseas talent from Asia. For now, Turner remains the incumbent, and Kim is only a reported scouting target. But as Kim continues to develop his star talent in KBO with an MLB transition on the horizon. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: The six Illinois basketball home games I’m most excited to attend
item.description: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 17: Head coach Brad Underwood of the Illinois Fighting Illini walks off the court after an exhibition game against the Cincinnati Bearcats at Fifth Third Arena on October 17, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Illinois basketball is almost back. The home schedule is loaded. Football is 3-3 and frustrating me every Saturday. I’m ready to be back in State Farm Center. This isn’t a ranking of the six most important home games. It’s the six I’m most excited to attend. Maybe it’s a big opponent. Maybe there’s an NBA prospect I want to see. Maybe Scottie Pippen’s kid is playing. Maybe it’s just November, and I’ve spent seven months without Illinois basketball. Here we go. 6. Fairleigh Dickinson — Nov. 2 Why am I excited to see Fairleigh Dickinson? Because it’s Nov. 2, and there will be an Illinois basketball game happening in front of me. That’s it. There are only so many times during an offseason I can look at roster updates, watch clips of new guys and convince myself that THIS is definitely the year before I need to see an actual basketball game. FDU is the first one that counts. They could play the Washington Generals on opening night, and I’d probably have them sixth on this list. 5. Penn State — Dec. 12 Now the games start getting real. Illinois actually opens Big Ten play four days earlier at Minnesota, but Penn State is the first conference team coming to Champaign. And there’s just something about that first Big Ten home game. By this point, Illinois will have already played Texas Tech, Duke and UConn. We’ll have had more than a month to wildly overreact to every good and bad thing this team does. Then Penn State comes to town, and conference season is officially in the building. Penn State basically rebuilt its roster, but there’s one guy I’m interested in seeing: Roko Prkačin. He’s a 6-foot-8 Croatian (my friend Luke will probably love that) who has already played professional basketball in Europe and for Croatia’s senior national team. So while most college players were worrying about chemistry homework, this guy was playing grown men overseas. That’s interesting. But let’s not overcomplicate this. It’s the Big Ten home opener. That’s why it’s here. 4. Michigan State — Feb. 5 Michigan State could show up with five random dudes from the East Lansing YMCA, and I’d probably still want to go. It’s Michigan State. It’s Tom Izzo. It’s Illinois. It’s Friday night at State Farm Center. But they don’t have five random YMCA guys. They have Jeremy Fears Jr. And that guy is a problem. Fears averaged 15.2 points and 9.4 assists, along with, unofficially, a concerning number of trips and groin shots last season. Seriously, what does this guy have against ankles and future children? Illinois got the full Jeremy Fears experience last year when he went for 26 points and 15 assists in Michigan State’s overtime win over the Illini. Now he’s the preseason Big Ten Player of the Year. Michigan
item.content:encoded: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 17: Head coach Brad Underwood of the Illinois Fighting Illini walks off the court after an exhibition game against the Cincinnati Bearcats at Fifth Third Arena on October 17, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Illinois basketball is almost back. The home schedule is loaded. Football is 3-3 and frustrating me every Saturday. I’m ready to be back in State Farm Center. This isn’t a ranking of the six most important home games. It’s the six I’m most excited to attend. Maybe it’s a big opponent. Maybe there’s an NBA prospect I want to see. Maybe Scottie Pippen’s kid is playing. Maybe it’s just November, and I’ve spent seven months without Illinois basketball. Here we go. 6. Fairleigh Dickinson — Nov. 2 Why am I excited to see Fairleigh Dickinson? Because it’s Nov. 2, and there will be an Illinois basketball game happening in front of me. That’s it. There are only so many times during an offseason I can look at roster updates, watch clips of new guys and convince myself that THIS is definitely the year before I need to see an actual basketball game. FDU is the first one that counts. They could play the Washington Generals on opening night, and I’d probably have them sixth on this list. 5. Penn State — Dec. 12 Now the games start getting real. Illinois actually opens Big Ten play four days earlier at Minnesota, but Penn State is the first conference team coming to Champaign. And there’s just something about that first Big Ten home game. By this point, Illinois will have already played Texas Tech, Duke and UConn. We’ll have had more than a month to wildly overreact to every good and bad thing this team does. Then Penn State comes to town, and conference season is officially in the building. Penn State basically rebuilt its roster, but there’s one guy I’m interested in seeing: Roko Prkačin. He’s a 6-foot-8 Croatian (my friend Luke will probably love that) who has already played professional basketball in Europe and for Croatia’s senior national team. So while most college players were worrying about chemistry homework, this guy was playing grown men overseas. That’s interesting. But let’s not overcomplicate this. It’s the Big Ten home opener. That’s why it’s here. 4. Michigan State — Feb. 5 Michigan State could show up with five random dudes from the East Lansing YMCA, and I’d probably still want to go. It’s Michigan State. It’s Tom Izzo. It’s Illinois. It’s Friday night at State Farm Center. But they don’t have five random YMCA guys. They have Jeremy Fears Jr. And that guy is a problem. Fears averaged 15.2 points and 9.4 assists, along with, unofficially, a concerning number of trips and groin shots last season. Seriously, what does this guy have against ankles and future children? Illinois got the full Jeremy Fears experience last year when he went for 26 points and 15 assists in Michigan State’s overtime win over the Illini. Now he’s the preseason Big Ten Player of the Year. Michigan State also has Coen Carr, who is basically what happens when somebody maxes out the athleticism sliders in 2K. But Fears is the guy I want to watch. There’s also a little revenge factor here. You can’t come in, drop 26 and 15 on my team and expect me to forget about it. Here’s hoping the Illini wear their protective cups and do something about it this season. 3. UCLA — Feb. 2 We’re a couple of years into this now, and I still haven’t completely processed UCLA being in the Big Ten. UCLA. Los Angeles. Big Ten. Whatever. I’m just going to accept it. And I’m especially willing to accept it when they bring somebody like Nikola Kusturica to Champaign. Remember that name. Kusturica is a 6-foot-9 Serbian wing who came through FC Barcelona’s basketball system and absolutely destroyed the FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup. He averaged 24.6 points and 6.9 rebounds. Then Serbia played Team USA in the gold-medal game, and he scored 37 freaking points. He’s so young that he isn’t even eligible for the 2027 NBA Draft. We’re talking 2028. And there are already people putting him near the top of that draft class. Now, projecting an NBA Draft two years in advance is basically basketball astrology, so who knows what happens between now and then? But that’s exactly why I want to see him. There’s a chance we’re sitting in Champaign watching a future top-five NBA pick before most people in America know who he is. If he becomes a star, I get to be annoying five years from now and tell people I watched him play at State Farm Center when he was a teenager. That’s worth the price of admission by itself. 2. Ohio State — Jan. 9 First, there’s Anthony Thompson. He’s a 6-foot-9 five-star freshman, a McDonald’s All-American and one of the top recruits in the country. He’s Ohio State’s highest-rated recruit since Jared Sullinger. That’s saying something. He’s already showing up on 2027 NBA Draft boards, so there’s a legitimate chance we’re watching a future first-round pick. Then things get fun. Ohio State has Justin Pippen. Scottie Pippen’s son. And Justin can actually play. He averaged 14.2 points and 4.6 assists at Cal last year before transferring to Ohio State. Then they have Myles Herro. Tyler Herro’s little brother. They also have one of my favorites to watch, John Mobley Jr., who averaged 15.7 points last season while shooting better than 41% from 3-point range. So we’re getting a five-star future NBA prospect, Scottie Pippen’s kid, Tyler Herro’s brother and one of the better returning guards in the Big Ten. It’s also Illinois-Ohio State. That is an easy No. 2 for me. 1. USC — Jan. 27 This roster is ridiculous. Let’s start with Alijah Arenas. Gilbert Arenas’ son. And if you’re around my age, Gilbert Arenas was one of those guys you absolutely remember. Agent Zero. Dude was pulling up from everywhere before everybody in the NBA decided they needed to shoot 10 3s a game. Now his 6-foot-7 son is coming to Champaign. Alijah was a five-star recruit and has legitimate NBA potential himself. His freshman season got derailed by a terrifying car accident and later a knee injury, but once he actually got healthy, you could see why he had so much hype. That’s already enough to make USC interesting. Then they added Christian Collins, a 6-foot-9 McDonald’s All-American and one of the best freshmen in the country. USC also has Adonis and Darius Ratliff. They’re twins. They’re the sons of Theo Ratliff. Adonis is 6-foot-11. Darius is 7 feet. Both were McDonald’s All-Americans. So USC is coming to State Farm Center with three sons of former NBA All-Stars on the same roster. Gilbert Arenas’ kid. Theo Ratliff’s two giant kids. Plus Christian Collins. Plus Rodney Rice. Plus KJ Lewis. Plus Jacob Cofie, another 6-foot-10 guy who has gotten some NBA attention. This isn’t a college basketball roster. This is the cast of a basketball movie where every character gets introduced with a graphic explaining who his dad is. And that’s exactly why it’s No. 1. I want to see these guys in person. Again, these aren’t necessarily the six biggest home games. I’m ready for Nov. 2. I’m ready to walk back into State Farm Center. I’m ready to convince myself after one 12-0 run against Fairleigh Dickinson that Illinois is winning the national championship. College basketball is almost back. Thank God.

item.title: Maple Leafs’ Gavin McKenna gets candid about scoring game winning goal amid media pressure
item.description: Gavin McKenna delivered a timely response to the pressure surrounding his rookie NHL season, scoring the game-winning goal in the Toronto Maple Leafs ’ 3-1 victory over the San Jose Sharks on Monday. The 2026 No. 1 overall pick scored on a third-period power play, helping Toronto snap a three-game losing streak. The goal also came during McKenna’s first NHL meeting against No. 2 pick Ivar Stenberg. Speaking to Sportsnet after the game, McKenna explained what the decisive goal meant to him. “That one felt good. Tight game, so yeah, to kind of get the boys going with that one, it felt pretty good,” McKenna said. MORE: Maple Leafs announce massive shakeup, series of roster moves ahead of Sharks matchup The 18-year-old has faced intense scrutiny since arriving in Toronto. Every performance has attracted attention, particularly after his early struggles and limited ice time during the recent loss to Buffalo. However, McKenna appeared comfortable discussing the spotlight when David Amber asked about playing as Toronto’s top draft pick. “It’s been a lot of fun,” McKenna said. “Obviously, the media is always on you, whether it’s good or bad, but I’ve had a lot of fun.” Gavin McKenna embraces Toronto’s demanding spotlight Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Toronto Maple Leafs left wing Gavin McKenna arrives before a game at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) McKenna also praised the support he has received from the city and its fans. “This place has been awesome to me. I’m feeling the support from the fans, and it’s an unreal hockey city. So I’ve been loving my time here,” he added. "I've had a lot of fun. This place has been awesome to me." 💙 Gavin McKenna chats with the panel after scoring the game-winning goal in Toronto's win. pic.twitter.com/IqgYvWCTBz — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 20, 2026 McKenna’s response suggests he understands the expectations attached to playing in one of hockey’s most passionate markets. That attitude matters as he adjusts to the NHL’s speed and physical demands. Toronto also needs its young forward to contribute consistently rather than carry the offense alone. Auston Matthews recorded a goal and two assists against San Jose, while Sergei Bobrovsky made 30 saves. MORE: Maple Leafs coach takes blame for benching Gavin McKenna in OT loss The victory provides McKenna and the Maple Leafs with momentum after a difficult stretch. His game-winner will ease some immediate pressure, but maintaining that progress remains the bigger challenge. Toronto faces Columbus on Tuesday, giving McKenna another opportunity to build on his latest performance. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Highest-Paid NBA Players 2026: Curry Is Basketball’s First $200 Million Man
item.description: Stephen Curry was the NBA’s first unanimous MVP, in 2016. The first player to lead the league in 3-pointers four times, then five times, then six and seven and eight times. The first player to launch 10,000 attempts from beyond the arc—and the first to drain 4,000 of them. But for all of the ways the Golden State Warriors’ 38-year-old sharpshooter has transformed basketball, he is just as much of a game-changer financially. item.content:encoded: Stephen Curry was the NBA’s first unanimous MVP, in 2016. The first player to lead the league in 3-pointers four times, then five times, then six and seven and eight times. The first player to launch 10,000 attempts from beyond the arc—and the first to drain 4,000 of them. But for all of the ways the Golden State Warriors’ 38-year-old sharpshooter has transformed basketball, he is just as much of a game-changer financially. Already the first NBA player with a $40 million salary ( in 2019-20 ) and a $50 million salary ( 2023-24 ), Curry is set to cross the $60 million threshold this season, banking $62.6 million on the court. Meanwhile, after splitting with his longtime sponsor Under Armour last fall and unveiling a new deal with Chinese shoe brand Li-Ning in June, Curry projects to earn an estimated $141 million from endorsements and other business endeavors—demolishing the NBA-record $100 million he made off the court in 2024-25. Put the two numbers together, and Curry is poised to haul in $203.6 million over the coming year, becoming the first active NBA player to surpass $200 million. In fact, since Forbes began tracking athlete income in 1990, only three other sports stars have cleared that bar in the course of 12 months (unadjusted for inflation): boxer Floyd Mayweather, soccer legend Cristiano Ronaldo and golfer Jon Rahm. Forbes The historic windfall keeps Curry on top of Forbes’ list of the highest-paid NBA players for the second straight year . LeBron James, who led the ranking for 11 consecutive seasons before slipping to No. 2 in 2025, now slides to No. 4 with an estimated $93.9 million after signing with the Philadelphia 76ers in July for the veteran’s minimum of $3.9 million this season. Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant, due to collect an estimated $104.9 million, and Giannis Antetokounmpo, who will pocket a total of $103.5 million after being traded to the Miami Heat over the summer, slot in ahead of James on this year’s list. Together, the NBA’s ten highest-paid players are expected to bring in $958 million this season before taxes and agent fees, a 6% increase from the 2025 list’s record $902 million and more than double the $449 million total from a decade ago. The group’s combined $469 million in off-court income is nearly $90 million beyond last year’s record $380 million—and light years ahead of the comparable numbers for the ten highest-paid athletes in other sports like soccer ( $281 million ), MLB ( $144 million ), the NFL ( $84 million ) and the NHL ( $16 million ). And while the $489 million this year’s top ten are earning on the court is down from the past two seasons, that is almost entirely a function of the 41-year-old James’ “ last decision ” to accept less money for a shot at another championship as his illustrious career winds down. The NBA’s salary cap is set at $165 million this season, up 75% from ten years ago, as strong growth across the league’s business drives up the value of players’ roughly 50% share of basketball-related income, as ensured by their collective bargaining agreement. A decade ago, as some league observers fretted that a one-year cap spike had produced out-of-whack contracts, James had the NBA’s highest salary at $31 million. This season, 59 NBA players are set to exceed that mark, according to Spotrac . Still, after an 11-year, $76 billion national broadcast package that was signed in 2024 and began last season led some around the league to assume the salary cap would jump by the maximum of 10% for the foreseeable future, the reality has been a bit less robust . This season, the cap climbed by 6.7%, and it is projected to rise by a similar percentage in 2027-28. Hampering the growth is the turbulence in the local media market, after the collapse of regional sports network operator Main Street Sports Group cost 16 NBA teams tens of millions of dollars in annual revenue—each. Don’t expect that hurdle to halt the players’ financial fast break, however. While Curry’s salary is set to dip back below $60 million next season after he gave the Warriors a break with the two-year, $116 million contract extension he signed in September—$20.7 million less than the maximum that was available to him—there are more money milestones in the NBA’s future. For starters, the league is on track to crack the $70 million barrier in 2029-30—with at least three different players . THE HIGHEST-PAID NBA PLAYERS 2026 #1. $203.6 million Stephen Curry Age: 38 | Position: Point Guard | Team: Golden State Warriors | On-Court: $62.6 million • Off-Court: $141 million Ezra Shaw/Getty Images After becoming the first active player to be the subject of a dedicated exhibit at the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in July, Curry heads into his 18th pro season still able to dominate a game. In the NBA’s annual survey of general managers , the four-time champion was recently named the league’s best pure shooter, with 97% of the vote, and despite the creaky knees that come with being 38 years old, he was labeled the best at moving without the ball by 80% of the voters. Curry is similarly making his impact felt in the retail world: His new partnership with China’s Li-Ning is reportedly worth $400 million over ten years, with a signature shoe due to be released early next year. Meanwhile, Under Armour, the former home of his Curry Brand sneakers, said in May that it expected its annual revenue to fall 1% because of the company’s split with the longtime face of its basketball business. Curry, whose other sponsors include Chase, Rakuten and new addition Glaukos, is one of only five active athletes ever to have reached $100 million with their off-court income in a single year, alongside golfer Tiger Woods , tennis player Roger Federer , MMA fighter Conor McGregor and Los Angeles Dodgers two-way phenom Shohei Ohtani . He was also featured in the documentary Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry , which was released this month on IMAX screens and depicts the 2025 game in which he made his 4,000th career 3-pointer. #2. $104.9 million Kevin Durant Age: 38 | Position: Forward | Team: Houston Rockets | On-Court: $43.9 million • Off-Court: $61 million Ronald Martinez/Getty Images Durant signed a two-year, $90 million contract extension last October, sacrificing around $30 million to give the Houston Rockets financial flexibility to build their roster, but he is still poised to surpass LeBron James as the NBA’s all-time on-court earnings leader in 2027-28, which will take him to $591 million for his career. The 38-year-old forward could also potentially widen the gap by declining his player option for next season and returning to free agency in the summer of 2027. Off the court, Durant has endorsement deals with brands including CeraVe, Dick’s Sporting Goods and FanDuel and invests through his family office 35V, which reportedly had a major score recently when Nvidia agreed to acquire AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion. Durant is also a cofounder of media company Boardroom, which agreed to a distribution and ad-sales deal with Wondery in June; starting early next year, Boardroom’s podcasts will be available across Amazon services, including Amazon Music, Prime Video and Fire TV Channels. #3. $103.5 million Giannis Antetokounmpo Age: 31 | Position: Forward | Team: Miami Heat | On-Court: $58.5 million • Off-Court: $45 million Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images Traded to the Miami Heat over the summer after 13 years with the Milwaukee Bucks, Antetokounmpo said recently of playing in front of a new fan base: “I feel energized. I feel alive.” Another bonus of the move: Relocating from Wisconsin to Florida, which has no state income tax, could save the 31-year-old forward millions through his next contract, which he could sign as an extension starting in January . (Alternatively, he could decline his player option for 2027-28 and become a free agent next summer.) With partnerships with more than a dozen brands, including recent deals wi

item.title: Shannon Sharpe hammers ‘dirty’ San Francisco 49ers player for injuring his opponent
item.description: Photo by Marcus Ingram/Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers secured themselves at least another week with their unbeaten status following their victory over the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. Kyle Shanahan’s team are now 6-0 through the opening six weeks of the season but their win on Monday did not come without criticism. It was by no means a flawless performance from the Niners as they had to battle a late comeback from the Commanders. There was also a moment of controversy during the game in Santa Clara that saw Niners rookie defensive lineman Gracen Halton heavily criticised online for a dirty play. Halton dove into the left knee of Commanders offensive lineman Sam Cosmi which saw him ruled out of the game. With the ball nowhere near Cosmi’s vicinity, this play from Halton has been labelled as dirty and Shannon Sharpe has led the online frustrations. Shannon Sharpe hits out at San Francisco 49ers’ Gracen Halton over dirty play The Niners did secure the victory in the end but it has come slightly tarnished for some given the manner in which some of their players conducted themselves at Levi’s Stadium. Halton has come under a lot of criticism for his actions that ended Cosmi’s game. “Dirty A** play by 93 of the 49ers. That’s bush league. Could really injure that man,” said Sharpe on X. The referees did throw a flag down on the play and penalised Halton for a low block which meant a half-the-distance-to-the-goal ruling. However, Cosmi was unable to return to the game which was a real blow for the Commanders. Cosmi headed straight into the blue tent and did not play again on the night. Sharpe’s frustrations will have been shared by fans across the nation given Halton was never going to make a play on the running back with possession of the ball. Commanders fans will now be hoping the injury is nothing serious for Cosmi. Read more: NFL Network analyst apologises to Jalen Hurts after controversial comments over missing 2026 season ESPN’s efforts to change Jason Kelce look to have failed after ‘epic’ Monday Night Football moment Washington Commanders loss makes NFL history as NFC East sets embarrassing record

item.title: Full timeline of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot issues after Eagles QB ruled out for the 2026 NFL season
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles QB Jalen Hurts will not play another game in the 2026 NFL season after being ruled out with deep-vein thrombosis and blood clots in his lungs. The Eagles have started the season 2-4 and been at the centre of a negative media spotlight, suffering multiple injury setbacks as well as being on pace for their first losing season in over half a decade. Hurts was under fire for his disappointing performances through the first few weeks, but the Eagles’ actions in managing a potential injury to their star QB amid an injury crisis which demolished most of their team are now under the spotlight. Jalen Hurts injury timeline starts with Week 4 loss to Rams and ends with season-ending news The beginning of Hurts’ injury merry-go-round came with their 24-20 loss to the Rams, where Hurts was cleated in the calf, but did not request treatment until a few days later, remaining a full practice participant in the interim. The Eagles flew to London for an international game against the Jacksonville Jaguars for Week 5. Despite the presence of superficial blood clots in Hurts’ calf, he was cleared to play in the high-stakes game. Despite the situation being bad enough for Hurts to avoid getting a full night’s rest before the game and playing on just a few intermittent hours of sleep, he played in their 19-17 loss, shouldering the blame for the result. With flights being a major health risk for people with blood clots, Hurts still took the trans-Atlantic flight to return to Philadelphia, immediately getting back into the routine of practising with his teammates. However, a follow-up ultrasound proved that the superficial calf clot had moved, ruling him out for their Week 6 clash against the Carolina Panthers, which ended with a 25-14 loss. After further testing on October 19, it was revealed that Hurts had multiple blood clots in both lungs and was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), ruling him out for the rest of the season. Many fans and experts are criticising how the Eagles handled Hurts’ injury, including the blood clot discovery in London and advising him to play on limited rest and fly back to the USA after the game. His consistent presence in practice was also criticised, as the Eagles should have stepped in to protect the 28-year-old QB from a potentially life-threatening situation. With Hurts expected to recover after a course of blood thinners, everyone is hoping the former Super Bowl Champion can come into the 2027 NFL season as the best version of himself, putting the problems from this season behind him. item.title: Uncapped Dragons get Wales Nations Championship call
item.description: Aneurin Owen and Che Hope have featured in the opening four games of 2026-27 for Dragons [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Uncapped Dragons centre Aneurin Owen and scrum-half Che Hope have been included in Wales' squad for the Nations Championship. Steve Tandy has selected a 39-strong group for the November Tests, with hooker Dewi Lake named as captain. The head coach calls up Dragons lock Seb Davies and Cardiff number eight Taine Basham for the first time since he took charge of the national side. Cardiff loose-head prop Rhys Barratt, who played in the summer fixture against the Barbarians, is the third uncapped player in the squad, while Dragons wing Rio Dyer earns a recall. Leicester flanker Tommy Reffell and fit-again number eight Taulupe Faletau are among the notable absentees. Wales face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff and finish against a southern hemisphere opponent on finals weekend at Twickenham. Will Wales tackle reliance on Williams before World Cup? Ref Whitehouse retires to join Wales coaching team Owen was a member of the Wales squad in the summer of 2021 but did not feature in the Tests against Canada or Argentina. The 26-year-old from Newport has been a key member of the Dragons side that has built on an encouraging 2025-26 with a promising start to the season. Owen gets his chance in the absence of injured Cardiff centre Ben Thomas to join Eddie James, Joe Hawkins, Max Llewellyn and Louie Hennessey as a midfield option. Hope, 23, is brought in for a first taste of international camp and joins Tomos Williams and Reuben Morgan-Williams, with Kieran Hardy facing a lengthy lay-off after a knee injury. There is no place for in-form Scarlets wing Macs Page, but Dragons' Dyer, who has also started the season strongly, does earn a recall. The 26-year-old won the most recent of his 24 caps against South Africa last November. Leicester's Gabriel Hamer-Webb, who made his Wales debut against Scotland in the Six Nations, also returns after missing out in the summer. Lock Davies, who moved from Cardiff to Dragons in the summer of 2025, will aim to win his first cap since the 2022 Six Nations. Dynamic back-row forward Basham has started the season strongly for Cardiff and gets the nod ahead of fit-again Faletau, who made his first appearance of the season for Cardiff at Northampton on Sunday. Belcher gets the nod ahead of Elliot Dee, the leading try scorer in the United Rugby Championship (URC), as the third hooker behind captain Lake and Ryan Elias. Tandy said: "It's great to welcome back the players who were unavailable for the first three rounds of the Nations Championship. There is a round of URC action this weekend and back-row forward Taine Plumtree and centre Hawkins have been allowed to travel to South Africa with Scarlets for their fixture against Stormers on Saturday. Wales great Evans to leave role as Lions chairman Wales Nations Championship squad Forwards: Rhys Barratt, Rhys Carre, Nicky Smith, Gareth Thomas, Dewi Lake (capt), Liam Belcher, Ryan Elias, Tomas Francis, Archie Griffin, Dillon Lewis, Adam Beard, Ben Carter, Seb Davies, Dafydd Jenkins, Teddy Williams, Taine Basham, James Botham, Kane James, Alex Mann, Jac Morgan, Taine Plumtree, Aaron Wainwright. item.title: Pauls aims for December fight as bout is cancelled
item.description: Brad Pauls was the first boxer from Cornwall to win a British title since 1939 when he won in July 2024 [Getty Images] Former British and IBF international middleweight champion Brad Pauls said he is trying to find a fight before the end of the year. The 33-year-old was due to box on 13 November, but the bout has been cancelled. Newquay's Pauls lost his IBF International belt to Bradley Goldsmith in his last fight in June - just his third defeat in a 25-fight professional career that has seen him draw once. Pauls knocked out highly-rated Shakiel Thompson in March and had been hoping for a world title fight. "I'm absolutely gutted," Pauls said on social media. "It's not ideal, but we have to scramble and try to find a new date to fight before Christmas. "We're looking at a few, possibly just a couple weeks into December, which I'll announce properly soon." Pauls 'absolutely gutted' after Goldsmith defeat Pauls eyes world title shot after Thompson knockout Pauls won the British title in July 2024 when he stopped Nathan Heaney in a rematch, four months after the pair had drawn their first title fight. He went on to lose a European title fight against Denzel Bentley in December 2024 and only fought once last year on a low-key card in Torquay, before returning to the big stage against Thompson. Pauls hopes he has another big fight lined up next year, making a bout this side of Christmas key to his preparations. "It's massively important I fight again before the end of the year," he added. "I've got a bigger fight lined up for February time, back on the big stage, and I want to give myself every advantage for these big fights, so I need to be active and to get out before the end of the year." item.title: Pierre Sage faces sack after Crystal Palace's heaviest defeat in 70 years
item.description: Pierre Sage faces sack after Crystal Palace's heaviest defeat in 70 years Crystal Palace have the worst defensive record in the Premier League right now, having conceded eight goals in their last two games against Lyon and Brighton. The Eagles' collapse at the Amex Stadium was particularly painful, after shipping three goals in the opening 10 minutes on their way to a 5-0 defeat - their heaviest loss in 70 years. Pierre Sage has managed just two wins in his first seven Premier League games since replacing Oliver Glasner, and he is already under growing pressure. Despite enjoying success with Lens, where he guided the club to second place in Ligue 1 and won the Coupe de France, the Frenchman is struggling to get his ideas across at Selhurst Park. There are also signs of unrest within the dressing room. According to Standard Sport , several players have become frustrated with Sage’s communication and methods. Tensions reportedly emerged as early as September, following his decision to drop centre-back Jaydee Canvot after a 3-2 home defeat to Ipswich. Sage has admitted feeling ashamed of the Brighton performance and conceded that he does not know whether he will be given more time to turn things around. Defender Chris Richards also apologised to supporters after the defeat, admitting he felt embarrassed and emotional about the result. With Palace exploring potential replacements, the coming week could prove decisive for Sage. Matches against Besiktas and Newcastle offer him a chance to respond, but the pressure is mounting and results will need to improve quickly if he is to keep his job.
