Tensions reportedly emerged as early as September, following his decision to drop centre-back Jaydee Canvot after a 3-2 home defeat to Ipswich. Sage has admitted feeling ashamed of the Brighton performance and conceded that he does not know whether he will be given more time to turn things around. Defender Chris Richards also apologised to supporters after the defeat, admitting he felt embarrassed and emotional about the result. With Palace exploring potential replacements, the coming week could prove decisive for Sage. Matches against Besiktas and Newcastle offer him a chance to respond, but the pressure is mounting and results will need to improve quickly if he is to keep his job.

item.title: Real Madrid midfielder could play in makeshift role in El Clasico vs Barcelona
item.description: Real Madrid midfielder could play in makeshift role in El Clasico vs Barcelona Federico Valverde’s position is shaping up to be one of the key tactical questions for Real Madrid ahead of their trip to Barcelona on Sunday. According to MARCA , the Real Madrid captain is expected to feature out wide again, but whether he starts at right-back or in a more advanced role remains uncertain. Real Madrid’s victory over Sevilla brought several positives, with Valverde’s performance at right-back among the most encouraging. After impressing in the same position during the Champions League comeback against AS Roma, he delivered another solid display, strengthening his case as an alternative in a role where neither Trent Alexander-Arnold nor Denzel Dumfries has fully convinced. Valverde’s versatility could be key Dumfries is expected to start at right-back against RB Leipzig on Wednesday, but the bigger question is where Valverde will play in Sunday’s Clasico at the Spotify Camp Nou. Subject to what happens in the Champions League, the signs point towards the Madrid captain featuring on the right flank against the league leaders. Another shift at right-back? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Arda Guler’s performances in the double pivot have provided Real Madrid with an important source of creativity, with Aurelien Tchouameni offering defensive protection alongside the Turkish midfielder. That leaves Mourinho with a decision to make over Valverde’s starting position. The question is not necessarily which side of the pitch he will occupy, but how high up the flank he will operate. Playing at right-back remains a possibility, but Valverde could also move further forward to act as a right winger, potentially forming a complementary partnership with Dumfries behind him. This would give Real Madrid a more defensively secure right flank while allowing Valverde to contribute in attack. It also appears unlikely that Mourinho will risk starting Endrick on the right wing against Barcelona. The Brazilian has shown that he can make an impact from the bench, as he did in Rome, but at this stage of his career he is better suited to the role of an impact substitute than a regular starting option in such a demanding fixture. Pace could be crucial Valverde could exploit Barcelona’s high-line playing as a winger. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Playing as a winger would be nothing new for Valverde, who has occupied that position on numerous occasions during his Real Madrid career, particularly under Carlo Ancelotti. With Dumfries providing cover behind him, the Uruguayan would have greater freedom to attack the spaces ahead of him. His power, pace and long stride make him particularly effective when driving into open areas, potentially giving Real Madrid another weapon against Barcelona. item.title: Patriots injury analysis: O-line left in shambles after Jets game
item.description: The New England Patriots have started hitting their strides. Winning three games in a row, they again look like one of the best teams in football and a serious contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. At the same time, however, they continue being followed by some bad injury luck. Their 26-19 win over the New York Jets on Sunday saw multiple players exit with injury, including one — wide receiver Romeo Doubs — who has since been placed on injured reserve and will therefore be out at least four games. Receiver depth is not the only concern, however, as a look at our weekly injury analysis after rewatching the game shows. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 6 WR Romeo Doubs: On the second offensive snap of the day, Doubs was able to get open behind the Jets defense and haul in a 42-yard touchdown pass from Drake Maye. However, he came down hard on his shoulder while completing the catch and remained kneeling in the end zone afterwards. He ultimately did get up, but headed straight into the blue medical tent and later the locker room with a shoulder injury. He never returned. RT Morgan Moses: While most of the initial attention on the unsuccessful deep ball to A.J. Brown in the early second quarter was on the receiver, it quickly shifted to the Patriots’ right tackle. Morgan Moses remained down on the ground. He had pushed Jets pass rusher David Bailey wide, and along the way appears to have awkwardly bended his right foot. The team captain limped off the field and into the medical tent. He later left for the locker room, briefly reemerged, but was ultimately shut down for good. LG Alijah Vera-Tucker: When the Patriots offense took the field with 1:23 left in the first half, Vera-Tucker was not in the lineup. Instead, the left guard had departed for the locker room with what later was announced as a hamstring injury. He did finish the previous drive, but came up hobbled after a Rhamondre Stevenson run for a loss of 2 yards. RG Ben Brown: Lining up at left guard in place of the injured Alijah Vera-Tucker, an unsuspecting Brown was rolled up from behind on a Drake Maye scramble early in the fourth quarter. He remained on the ground, with members of the medical staff and head coach Mike Vrabel tending to him on the field. He later had to be helped off the field by two trainers, and into the blue medical tent. The Patriots quickly ruled him out with a knee injury after that. ED Dre’Mont Jones: Already coming into the game with a shoulder injury, Jones stayed down on the ground after a pass midway through the fourth quarter. He was holding his knee and slow to get up, but did walk off under own power and returned after missing just two plays. What this means for the Patriots As noted above, Romeo Doubs’ shoulder injury has since forced the Patriots to move him to injured reserve — another blow to a wide receiver group that has struggled with stability to start the season. He will be out at least until New England’s Week 12 game at the Chargers. No less concerning is the state of an offensive line that, frankly, is in shambles right now. After already losing starting right guard Mike Onwenu and his replacement Greg Van Roten in back-to-back weeks, it also saw third-stringer Ben Brown go down. Fourth-string guard Matt Pryor, who was signed off the Cardinals’ practice squad in September, finished the game. At left guard, Alijah-Vera Tucker looked good to start his Patriots career but is now a question mark as well. With Brown replacing him and subsequently going down as well, third-stringer Walter Rouse played the final 14 snaps at the position. Then, there is Morgan Moses, who was spotted in a walking boot after the game. First-round rookie Caleb Lomu took his spot in the lineup and for a second straight week looked good in extended action. Lomu, of course, already had to enter the lineup in Week 5 after left tackle Will Campbell had suffered a game-ending knee sprain. It’s not all bad news, though. For starters, Campbell appears to be fine after his prior injury scare. Likewise, Moses was listed as a limited practice participant on Monday’s injury report . Additionally, only Romeo Doubs was moved to IR on Monday; as of Tuesday morning, Brown and Vera-Tucker remain on the 53-man team despite being assigned the non-participant label on the practice report — a potential positive sign for their long-term availability. That said, with the Patriots playing the Bears in Chicago on Thursday night, it would not be a surprise if New England was again forced to adapt its starting O-line one way or another.

item.title: Former Liverpool Goalkeeper Admits He Struggled to Meet Klopp’s Standards
item.description: Former Liverpool Goalkeeper Admits He Struggled to Meet Klopp’s Standards Adam Bogdan Reveals Liverpool Regrets, Klopp’s Intensity and Goalkeeping Struggles Former Liverpool goalkeeper Adam Bogdan has spoken candidly about his time at Anfield, the extraordinary demands of playing under Jürgen Klopp, the mistakes that affected his confidence and the decision he wishes he had made differently. Speaking to Alison Bender on the After The Final Whistle podcast, the former Hungary international reflected on joining Liverpool from Bolton Wanderers in 2015, adapting to an increasingly demanding training environment and the psychological pressures of representing one of football’s biggest clubs. His recollections provide a fascinating account of life inside Liverpool during a period of considerable change. Adam Bogdan Recalls Liverpool Transfer and Klopp’s Training Demands Bogdan was preparing to leave Bolton after eight years when Liverpool’s interest emerged. He and his pregnant wife were driving back to Hungary when his agent called. “I had a phone call from my agent that it looks like Liverpool is getting serious,” Bogdan recalled. “Of course it’s a bit of a wow, like it’s unbelievable, you know, you could be part of a club like that.” His introduction to Liverpool was physically demanding. After his daughter’s birth, Bogdan returned to Melwood before travelling with the squad to Australia. “Massive. Massive. Because physically it was just like you surviving. You’re trying your best.” He remembered struggling during a training rondo until Alberto Moreno eventually allowed him to escape. Bogdan also highlighted the relentless standards established by senior players. “The intensity of Jordan Henderson, the intensity of Milner,” he recalled, mentioning Philippe Coutinho and Roberto Firmino among the squad. When Klopp replaced Brendan Rodgers, those demands increased again. “I remember the first game in Tottenham I was on the bench and I just couldn’t believe like is it this possible.” Bogdan explained how Klopp and Mauricio Pochettino helped raise the physical standards of elite football. “It’s down to those guys, you know, Pochettino and Klopp to keep increasing.” He now draws on that experience in his role as sporting director, particularly the lessons surrounding recruitment, expectations and creating the right environment. item.content:encoded: Former Liverpool Goalkeeper Admits He Struggled to Meet Klopp’s Standards Adam Bogdan Reveals Liverpool Regrets, Klopp’s Intensity and Goalkeeping Struggles Former Liverpool goalkeeper Adam Bogdan has spoken candidly about his time at Anfield, the extraordinary demands of playing under Jürgen Klopp, the mistakes that affected his confidence and the decision he wishes he had made differently. Speaking to Alison Bender on the After The Final Whistle podcast, the former Hungary international reflected on joining Liverpool from Bolton Wanderers in 2015, adapting to an increasingly demanding training environment and the psychological pressures of representing one of football’s biggest clubs. His recollections provide a fascinating account of life inside Liverpool during a period of considerable change. Adam Bogdan Recalls Liverpool Transfer and Klopp’s Training Demands Bogdan was preparing to leave Bolton after eight years when Liverpool’s interest emerged. He and his pregnant wife were driving back to Hungary when his agent called. “I had a phone call from my agent that it looks like Liverpool is getting serious,” Bogdan recalled. “Of course it’s a bit of a wow, like it’s unbelievable, you know, you could be part of a club like that.” His introduction to Liverpool was physically demanding. After his daughter’s birth, Bogdan returned to Melwood before travelling with the squad to Australia. “Massive. Massive. Because physically it was just like you surviving. You’re trying your best.” He remembered struggling during a training rondo until Alberto Moreno eventually allowed him to escape. Bogdan also highlighted the relentless standards established by senior players. “The intensity of Jordan Henderson, the intensity of Milner,” he recalled, mentioning Philippe Coutinho and Roberto Firmino among the squad. When Klopp replaced Brendan Rodgers, those demands increased again. “I remember the first game in Tottenham I was on the bench and I just couldn’t believe like is it this possible.” Bogdan explained how Klopp and Mauricio Pochettino helped raise the physical standards of elite football. “It’s down to those guys, you know, Pochettino and Klopp to keep increasing.” He now draws on that experience in his role as sporting director, particularly the lessons surrounding recruitment, expectations and creating the right environment. Liverpool Goalkeeping Mistakes and Watford Controversy Bender raised the Watford match, when Bogdan’s handling error became a defining talking point of his Liverpool career. The goalkeeper recalled that he had finally begun feeling comfortable with the required physical standards. “I got to a point in December where I was already feeling like quite good, up to the level, up to the speed, up to everything.” He maintained that the incident involved a foul. “Yeah, it was a foul because he kicked it out of my hand, but the referee didn’t see it.” Bogdan acknowledged Liverpool’s difficulties during the match and subsequently suffered another setback when he conceded directly from a corner in an FA Cup fixture. He explained that his response to those mistakes became particularly damaging. “I was devastated and I think people could see it that I was so angry with myself.” For Bogdan, the psychological consequences were significant. “Sometimes you’re going to make a mistake in the second game. It’s how you react.” He believed the coaching staff could recognise his difficulties recovering emotionally. “He’s not that resilient and we can’t afford to have that.” Bender also asked about the scrutiny accompanying mistakes at Liverpool. Bogdan acknowledged that public criticism would continue, while emphasising the importance of creating another opportunity. Adam Bogdan Admits He Should Have Stayed Longer at Liverpool One of Bogdan’s clearest regrets concerns his decision to leave Liverpool on loan. With Hungary preparing for the European Championship, he initially requested a January move to secure regular football. Liverpool retained him because they needed three goalkeepers. By the following summer, he had decided to leave. “If I could go back and change something, I would have given myself more time.” Bender clarified whether he specifically meant more time at Liverpool, and Bogdan confirmed that he did. He explained that his second preseason had felt considerably more manageable. “Everything, the surroundings, the goalkeeping coach, everything was more comfortable so I could perform better.” However, Liverpool had signed Loris Karius, and Bogdan was unwilling to remain as third choice. “At 28 I didn’t want to be a third choice.” He subsequently joined Wigan Athletic, where a serious knee injury disrupted his career. The recovery proved exceptionally difficult. “I couldn’t progress with the rehab.” Bogdan eventually returned to Hungary for treatment and credited that period with helping his rehabilitation progress. Alisson, Anfield Pressure and Bogdan’s Honest Assessment Perhaps the most revealing part of Bender’s interview concerned the confidence required to succeed as a Liverpool goalkeeper. Bogdan described himself as a perfectionist and admitted that mistakes had always affected him deeply. “Every time I made a mistake in high-profile games, just had the same feeling in my stomach.” He contrasted his own reactions with those of Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker. “If let’s say Alisson makes a mistake he’s not going to affect him for the rest of the game and it’s not going to affect him for the next game.” Bogdan acknowledged the personal burden he experienced. “For me it always felt like the end of the world really.” Discussing the pressure of performing at Anfield and other major stadiums, he offered a particularly candid assessment. “At the very, very top you need to have an undoubtedly self-confidence.” He admitted that this quality had sometimes been missing from his own game. “When you were knocked down deep down, I didn’t have that undeniable confidence in myself.” His reflections underline the importance Bogdan places on resilience, emotional control and the support surrounding a goalkeeper. For Liverpool supporters, the interview offers a detailed account of his experiences during Klopp’s early months, the difficulties he encountered and the decisions he continues to reflect upon. Bogdan’s appreciation of Liverpool’s training standards and the lessons he learned at the club remain evident in his work today. Watch the full interview: Adam Bogdan speaks to Alison Bender on After The Final Whistle.

item.title: Erik ten Hag: Cristiano Ronaldo let the team down, and he let me down
item.description: Erik ten Hag: Cristiano Ronaldo let the team down, and he let me down Erik ten Hag says Cristiano Ronaldo "let the team down" during his time as Manchester United manager, revealing that the Portuguese forward told teammates to save their legs in training. The Dutchman had kept his counsel on United in the two years since his sacking in October 2024. He broke that silence in a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic , conducted over two evenings in his hometown of Enschede, where he now works as technical director of FC Twente, his boyhood club. Ten Hag insisted his decision on Ronaldo was a rational one, despite his admiration for the player. He said he had travelled to Portugal to explain his plans to Ronaldo before taking the United job. Ronaldo had returned to Old Trafford in a high-profile transfer from Juventus in 2021, a summer before Ten Hag was appointed from Ajax. Despite an impressive first season prior to the new manager’s arrival, issues soon arose as Ronaldo’s ageing legs and Ten Hag’s tactics clashed. “Cristiano Ronaldo let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him. I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United. He's one of the best in history. I respected him a lot. But as a manager, I had to make a rational decision.” - Erik ten Hag to The Athletic The former United boss pointed to Ronaldo's approach on the training pitch, saying the forward had not done enough to get himself into shape. "He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself," Ten Hag said. "Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team." He added: "Cristiano Ronaldo was telling the players: save your legs at training. I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels." The interview also addressed the broken "promises" that Ten Hag believes led to his exit. He said selling Scott McTominay was ruled out in discussions with the board, only for a U-turn on the midfielder’s future. McTominay was later sold to Napoli for £25m and helped the Italian side to Serie A success in his debut season. Despite those frustrations, Ten Hag says he remains attached to the club. "I really want United to win. I want them to be successful again. I want the club to be back where it once was," he said.

item.title: Duncan Ferguson Returns To Management With Irish Premiership Side Glentoran
item.description: Duncan Ferguson Returns To Management With Irish Premiership Side Glentoran Irish Premiership side Glentoran have appointed former Everton striker Duncan Ferguson as their new First Team Manager on a multi-year contract, with Gary Bollan joining as assistant manager. The 54-year-old brings extensive Premier League playing and coaching experience to the Oval, having spent more than a decade in Everton’s coaching structure and twice taken caretaker charge of the Merseyside club. Ferguson progressed from Everton’s academy to the first-team staff in 2014, working under managers including Roberto Martínez, Ronald Koeman, Sam Allardyce, Marco Silva, Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benítez. His first spell as caretaker manager came in December 2019, when he guided Everton to a victory over Chelsea and draws against Manchester United and Arsenal. He subsequently became Ancelotti’s assistant, remained on the coaching staff under Benítez and took caretaker charge again in January 2022 before working alongside Frank Lampard. Ferguson left Everton in the summer of 2022 to pursue a managerial career of his own. He took charge of Forest Green Rovers in January 2023 before moving to Inverness Caledonian Thistle that September. His spell in Scotland ended in October 2024 following the club’s entry into administration. His previous managerial roles brought difficult challenges, including Forest Green’s relegation from League One and Inverness’s financial crisis. The Glentoran appointment offers him another opportunity to establish himself as a manager in his own right with a club used to challenging for major honours. “I am delighted to become manager of Glentoran. This is a big club with a tremendous history, and it is a great opportunity for me. I understand the responsibility that comes with the job,” Ferguson said. “I want to win trophies here. Glentoran should be challenging for the title and every cup and shield we enter. I know that success here will be judged on what we win.” Ferguson has also outlined his preferred style of play, saying he wants his side to attack with confidence while maintaining high standards in training and preparation. “I want us to play with confidence, get forward and give the supporters football they enjoy watching,” he said. “I am thorough in my preparation and expect a lot from my players.” Furthermore, Ferguson has confirmed that he intends to live in Belfast and build a long-term connection with the club and its supporters. “I have signed for the long term and will be living in Belfast. I want to get to know the people at the Club and in the wider community and become part of life here,” he said. Glentoran owner Ali Pour said the club had considered candidates from across the United Kingdom, Ireland and Scandinavia. He highlighted Ferguson’s football knowledge, coaching experience, leadership, approach to player development and recruitment, as well as his connections within the game. As a player, Ferguson represented Dundee United

I want to get to know the people at the Club and in the wider community and become part of life here,” he said. Glentoran owner Ali Pour said the club had considered candidates from across the United Kingdom, Ireland and Scandinavia. He highlighted Ferguson’s football knowledge, coaching experience, leadership, approach to player development and recruitment, as well as his connections within the game. As a player, Ferguson represented Dundee United, Rangers, Everton and Newcastle United, earning seven senior caps for Scotland. He scored 68 goals in 269 Premier League appearances and helped Everton win the FA Cup in 1995. The appointment also extends a longstanding link between Everton and Glentoran. Ferguson becomes the fifth former Everton player to manage the Belfast club, following David Reid, James McIntosh, Alex Young and Tommy Jackson. Billy Bingham, who played for both clubs, later managed Everton and led Northern Ireland to the 1982 and 1986 World Cup finals. Ferguson’s appointment brings considerable top-level experience to Glentoran, but his immediate challenge will be to translate that background into results in a competitive Irish Premiership and build a side capable of challenging for honours. If he can deliver a league title during his time in East Belfast, then legendary status awaits. However, Glentoran history suggests that is easier said than done.

item.title: Who is Ben Treloar? Australian umpire set to officiate in Ranji Trophy
item.description: Australian umpire Ben Treloar will officiate in two Ranji Trophy matches in India, while Indian umpire Parashar Joshi will travel to Australia to officiate in two Sheffield Shield matches and one One Day Cup game as part of the CA-BCCI Umpire Exchange Program. The program will give both umpires an opportunity to gain experience by officiating in domestic cricket competitions in each other's countries. Ben Treloar to officiate in two Ranji Trophy matches Treloar has officiated in 30 first-class matches, 20 List A matches and 39 Big Bash League games. He has also worked in two Women's One Day Internationals and four Women's T20 Internationals. Apart from his work as an umpire, Treloar serves as Cricket New South Wales' Umpire Education Officer. He helps train and develop future match officials. His work in umpire education has earned him four George Borwick Memorial Awards from the New South Wales Cricket Umpires and Scorers Association. Treloar will begin his India assignment with Delhi's Ranji Trophy match against Gujarat from October 18 to 21 in Delhi. He will then officiate in Mumbai's match against Haryana from October 26 to 29 in Mumbai. Parashar Joshi to officiate in Australia Joshi has experience across several Indian domestic cricket competitions. He has officiated in 19 first-class matches in the Ranji Trophy and Duleep Trophy, 32 List A matches in the Vijay Hazare Trophy and Deodhar Trophy, and 40 T20 matches. His T20 assignments include matches in the Indian Premier League and the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. Joshi's Australian assignment will begin with Queensland's Sheffield Shield match against Tasmania at the Gabba from November 11 to 14. He will then officiate in the One Day Cup match between the two teams at the same venue on November 16. His exchange program will conclude with the Sheffield Shield match between New South Wales and Queensland at the Sydney Cricket Ground from November 22 to 25.

item.title: Ten Hag Accuses Manchester United of Breaking Promises Before His Shock Sacking
item.description: Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images Erik ten Hag has accused Manchester United of breaking promises made after the 2024 FA Cup final, claiming the club failed to give him the support he expected before dismissing him in October. In an interview with The Athletic , the former Manchester United manager also questioned the timing of his sacking, arguing that the team’s performance data showed signs of progress. Ten Hag revealed that he opposed Scott McTominay’s sale but felt embarrassed and disappointed when the club went ahead with the transfer. He also pointed to leadership uncertainty after Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s INEOS group arrived and stressed the need for experienced signings to strengthen Manchester United’s squad. Despite his frustration, Ten Hag said he still wants Manchester United to succeed and urged the club to give interim manager Michael Carrick time to work. Manchester United Promises to Ten Hag Were Not Kept Ten Hag said Manchester United promised him loyalty, backing and better communication after the 2024 FA Cup final. The discussions took place in Ibiza, where he agreed to extend his contract by one year after initially refusing to continue with only 12 months remaining. “They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned,” Ten Hag said. “We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.” The former Manchester United manager pointed to Scott McTominay’s departure as a clear example of the club going against their agreement. “In Ibiza, we agreed. I said, ‘No selling Scott McTominay’,” Ten Hag explained. He argued that McTominay offered goals and a strong mentality, qualities he believed Manchester United needed. Ten Hag also highlighted the midfielder’s connection to the club. However, Manchester United sold McTominay, leaving Ten Hag disappointed with the decision and the lack of alignment between him and the club’s leadership. Ten Hag Questions Manchester United Sacking Timing Manchester United dismissed Ten Hag in late October 2024 after a defeat to West Ham left the team 14th in the Premier League table. However, he believes the club acted too quickly instead of allowing his work to develop. “I think it was quite weird to separate ways in that moment. All the data was showing we are good,” he said. item.content:encoded: Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images Erik ten Hag has accused Manchester United of breaking promises made after the 2024 FA Cup final, claiming the club failed to give him the support he expected before dismissing him in October. In an interview with The Athletic , the former Manchester United manager also questioned the timing of his sacking, arguing that the team’s performance data showed signs of progress. Ten Hag revealed that he opposed Scott McTominay’s sale but felt embarrassed and disappointed when the club went ahead with the transfer. He also pointed to leadership uncertainty after Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s INEOS group arrived and stressed the need for experienced signings to strengthen Manchester United’s squad. Despite his frustration, Ten Hag said he still wants Manchester United to succeed and urged the club to give interim manager Michael Carrick time to work. The discussions took place in Ibiza, where he agreed to extend his contract by one year after initially refusing to continue with only 12 months remaining. “They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned,” Ten Hag said. “We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.” The former Manchester United manager pointed to Scott McTominay’s departure as a clear example of the club going against their agreement. “In Ibiza, we agreed. I said, ‘No selling Scott McTominay’,” Ten Hag explained. He argued that McTominay offered goals and a strong mentality, qualities he believed Manchester United needed. Ten Hag also highlighted the midfielder’s connection to the club. However, Manchester United sold McTominay, leaving Ten Hag disappointed with the decision and the lack of alignment between him and the club’s leadership. Ten Hag Questions Manchester United Sacking Timing Manchester United dismissed Ten Hag in late October 2024 after a defeat to West Ham left the team 14th in the Premier League table. However, he believes the club acted too quickly instead of allowing his work to develop. “I think it was quite weird to separate ways in that moment. All the data was showing we are good,” he said. Ten Hag acknowledged that Manchester United had suffered poor results against Liverpool and Tottenham but argued that the team was beginning to improve its style of play. He also pointed out that the club remained involved in several cup competitions when the decision came. He considered the West Ham match one of the team’s better performances, despite the defeat. The former Manchester United manager also suggested that some people might have known about his dismissal before the official announcement. “I’m sure the process was already ongoing; there were already people — maybe even in the team — who knew what would happen the day after,” he said. Ten Hag also described the uncertainty surrounding the club after Ratcliffe’s INEOS group became involved. He said the ownership transition created disruption and made it harder for the manager to work effectively. He added that discussions about changing the managerial structure stopped after an initial meeting at Carrington, leaving him without clear answers about the club’s plans. Ten Hag Reveals Why Manchester United Needed Experienced Players Ten Hag believes Manchester United needed more experienced players who could deliver consistently and guide younger signings. He revealed that he pushed the club to pursue Harry Kane and Declan Rice. “I said to them, ‘I want only one player — and you know who’. I fought for it,” he said, referring to his efforts to sign Kane. Ten Hag also felt Manchester United could have done more to test the possibility of signing Rice. He believed players with their experience and quality would have strengthened the squad and helped younger teammates develop. Despite his criticism, Ten Hag insisted he still wants Manchester United to return to success. “I really want United to win. I want them to be successful again,” he said. He also urged the club to give Michael Carrick time rather than make decisions based on short-term results. Ten Hag’s comments underline his belief that Manchester United need consistent leadership, clear communication and a long-term plan rather than repeated changes in the dugout. item.title: FIFA bans three Egyptians over World Cup match incidents
item.description: FILE PHOTO: French referee Francois Letexier (L) speaks with the players after Egypt conceded their third goal during the 2026 FIFA World Cup Round of 16 match between Argentina and Egypt at Atlanta Stadium. (is associated with: «FIFA bans three Egyptians over World Cup match incidents») Tom Weller/dpa Egypt midfielder Mostafa Ziko has been banned for five matches and coach Hossam Hassan for three games over incidents after their World Cup elimination by Argentina, the Egypt FA has said. A statement said that team manager Ibrahim Hassan was also banned for three games by world governing body FIFA and that Egypt plans to appeal the sanctions. Tempers flared after the final whistle of the July 7 round of 16 match, with the Egyptian camp furious at French referee François Letexier and his assistants. Egypt lodged an official complaint at FIFA over the officiating the day after the match and wanted Letexier banned for the rest of the tournament. Their main complaint was that before Enzo Fernández's 3-2 winner in stoppage time Argentine player Alexis Mac Allister pulled down Hamdi Fathi in the penalty area at the other end for which Letexier did not award a penalty. Ziko had a goal for what would have been a 3-0 Egypt lead nullified because of a foul in the build-up.

item.title: Guardians dejected after ALCS Game 6 loss to Tampa Bay Rays
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG — A few minutes after the final out of the American League Championship Series was recorded, the Tampa Bay Rays were wildly celebrating on the field. Songs like “ This Is How We Roll ” and a number of others centered around the theme of sunshine blared over the PA system while champagne and confetti were sprayed across the outfield. At the same moment, inside the visiting clubhouse deep within the bowels of Tropicana Field, the Guardians were soaking in silence and dejection. The Rays beat Cleveland 7-3 in Game 6 of the ALCS , winning the series 4-2 and punching their ticket to the World Series, where the National League champion Milwaukee Brewers are waiting. After the final out, the Guardians were shielded from all of the pomp and circumstance of the Rays’ ALCS championship taking place on the field. But they were not shielded from the pain that accompanies such a loss and a brutally sudden end to a long playoff run in which the final stage was within their grasp. Virtually the only sound was the slapping of backs during hugs as players shared the hurt of the moment. Several sat at their assigned lockers staring into space, lost in a stunned silence. One pitcher entirely broke down into tears, knowing their run had come to an end. After a few minutes, he sat on a couch in the middle of the clubhouse, not wanting to leave. Two fellow pitchers sat on either side of the couch to reminisce about the journey they had just undertaken. After a while, a group of 7-8 players ended up making a circle with some chairs to continue talking and extend the night as far as possible before departing the ballpark, their last postgame bus ride of the season back to the hotel. After answering a few questions from reporters, manager Stephen Vogt walked back to the clubhouse. When he rounded the corner and headed down the hallway, he took his hat off in frustration and dejection. Before a group of people got to him, he put it back on and stood up straight. The skipper always puts on the brave face, even when times are tough on the ship. “I couldn’t be more proud of our group. It just hurts,” Vogt said, fighting back tears after being asked about his message to the team after the team. “It stings. Really felt like we had a team to go [all the way], and just weren’t able to get there. But I couldn’t be more proud of our entire group, our players, coaches, staff, front office. “Let it hurt. Let it sink in. Let it fuel you this winter. item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG — A few minutes after the final out of the American League Championship Series was recorded, the Tampa Bay Rays were wildly celebrating on the field. Songs like “ This Is How We Roll ” and a number of others centered around the theme of sunshine blared over the PA system while champagne and confetti were sprayed across the outfield. At the same moment, inside the visiting clubhouse deep within the bowels of Tropicana Field, the Guardians were soaking in silence and dejection. The Rays beat Cleveland 7-3 in Game 6 of the ALCS , winning the series 4-2 and punching their ticket to the World Series, where the National League champion Milwaukee Brewers are waiting. After the final out, the Guardians were shielded from all of the pomp and circumstance of the Rays’ ALCS championship taking place on the field. But they were not shielded from the pain that accompanies such a loss and a brutally sudden end to a long playoff run in which the final stage was within their grasp. Virtually the only sound was the slapping of backs during hugs as players shared the hurt of the moment. Several sat at their assigned lockers staring into space, lost in a stunned silence. One pitcher entirely broke down into tears, knowing their run had come to an end. After a few minutes, he sat on a couch in the middle of the clubhouse, not wanting to leave. Two fellow pitchers sat on either side of the couch to reminisce about the journey they had just undertaken. After a while, a group of 7-8 players ended up making a circle with some chairs to continue talking and extend the night as far as possible before departing the ballpark, their last postgame bus ride of the season back to the hotel. After answering a few questions from reporters, manager Stephen Vogt walked back to the clubhouse. When he rounded the corner and headed down the hallway, he took his hat off in frustration and dejection. Before a group of people got to him, he put it back on and stood up straight. The skipper always puts on the brave face, even when times are tough on the ship. “I couldn’t be more proud of our group. It just hurts,” Vogt said, fighting back tears after being asked about his message to the team after the team. “It stings. Really felt like we had a team to go [all the way], and just weren’t able to get there. But I couldn’t be more proud of our entire group, our players, coaches, staff, front office. “Let it hurt. Let it sink in. Let it fuel you this winter. But more than anything, just really proud of our group.” Cleveland Guardians reach ALCS in 2026 MLB playoffs When Vogt eventually made his way through the clubhouse, hugging players as he went and delivering messages of appreciation for a hard-fought year, he and Austin Hedges embraced for several moments in a bear hug. Perhaps nobody was more dejected after the loss than Hedges, who wore the face of someone who had been absolutely crushed by the result, and the ending of their 2026 story. And perhaps nobody embodied the 2026 Guardians quite like Hedges, whom president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti said “personifies what it means to be a great teammate and a winning player.” If there wasn’t a bus to catch back to the hotel, and if the Tropicana Field cleanup crew hadn’t needed to clear out he room, Hedges might have stayed in his seat until the morning, soaking in every ounce of their run before taking off the uniform. “It hurts,” Hedges said, visibly emotional. “I felt like this was a group that could win the World Series. Heck of a year. Tough to say goodbye.” Even into late August, very few people outside of the Guardians clubhouse viewed them as a real contender in October. They punched their way to within two wins of the World Series, substituting being viewed as a powerhouse with a resiliency that became not only their calling card, but their biggest point of pride. But in the end, it wasn’t enough. In the ALCS Game 6 loss, Junior Caminero appeared to deliver the dagger with a two-run home run off the left-field foul pole that gave the Rays a four-run lead. But, just after, the Guardians cut the deficit in half and had the go-ahead run on first base. A strikeout by Brayan Rocchio ended that rally, and the Rays' Yandy Diaz added the exclamation point with another back-breaking, two-run home run an inning later. “Obviously it’s disappointing. There’s really nothing else to say about it,” said Jo Adell , who had his first playoff experience this October. “We gave it all we had and just came up short. We didn’t get the job done. And this group of guys has been really something special and something I’ll never forget.” Their playoff journey came to an end two wins shy of the World Series, the deepest run since 2016. For the second time in three years, the Guardians were one of the final four teams standing. It’s an accomplishment of its own, especially considering their payroll and resources, but one dipped in bittersweet disappointment. “Yeah, I’m right there with them trying to make it to the World Series as well,” said Steven Kwan when asked about Cleveland fans waiting for a championship. “Definitely disappointing, and they’ve treated us so well. So, inching closer, but getting close isn’t achieving that goal.” Despite the Guardians making a great deal more noise than most would have expected back in June or July, their run through the playoffs ended with silence deep within Tropicana Field and the final stage of their journey painfully close but ultimately pushed out of their reach. Ryan Lewis covers the Guardians for the Beacon Journal. He can be reached at rlewis1@gannett.com. This article originally appeared on Akron Beacon Journal: Guardians dejected after ALCS Game 6 loss to Tampa Bay Rays

item.title: 'Step It Up' - Robin Roefs Issues Sunderland Demand After Bournemouth Shocker
item.description: Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs has called on the Black Cats to "step things up" and also have some honest conversations within the dressing room, following the deflating defeat at Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon. Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 , with Marcus Tavernier opening the scoring in the early exchanges after some horrific defensive work from Omar Alderete and Kevin Danso, which saw the Spurs loanee sent off just ten minutes later after another defensive mishap between the duo. The ten-men of Sunderland failed to wrestle back control against Marco Rose's side, and looked dishevelled defensively and out of ideas in the attacking third, with Bournemouth doubling their lead early in the second 45' after a tragic backpass from Alderete was easily intercepted to see Evanilson round Roefs and confirm the Cherries' victory. In truth, only Roefs and Nordi Mukiele could come out of Sunderland's performance with a shred of dignity, with the Dutch goalkeeper making several strong saves to keep the scoreline down despite the embarrassingly poor performance. Robin Roefs instructs Sunderland players against Bournemouth (IMAGO / Every Second Media) Robin Roefs Sends Sunderland Dressing Room Message After Bournemouth Mukiele had some strong words for Sunderland , suggesting that Regis Le Bris' side have potentially "become arrogant" this season, which would be the reason for their poor start, with the defeat on the south coast now the Black Cats' fourth consecutive Premier League loss within their opening seven of the campaign. Following Tottenham's win over Coventry City on Monday evening, Sunderland are now slumped to the foot of the Premier League table, placing substantial pressure on the Black Cats to get a victory when Leeds United travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday. With Sunderland heading for crisis stations, shot-stopper Roefs stressed that the Black Cats must have some "honest" conversations within the dressing room to resurrect their season, and that the onus is on the squad to match the increased expectations. And fast. As quoted by the Sunderland Echo , Roefs said: "We need to put the work in every day and not just today to make sure we turn this around and be honest with each other. Also keep the spirits up." On his individually decent display, he continued: "Well, obviously I don't care about this. It's just a team, “I don't think anyone today can walk off the pitch and say I was amazing today. It's just a team effort. It's not about me. It's not about our right-back, our left winger having a good game. "It's about the team. We all know this. We just need to step it up and make sure next week we turn it around. - "Obviously we didn't have the most easy games but we just gave away too many points against Ipswich, which we should have never lost. item.title: Tom Pelissero walks back Jalen Hurts no sleep claim after agent provides new details
item.description: NFL insider Tom Pelissero corrected his earlier account of Jalen Hurts ’ medical situation after the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback’s agent clarified what happened before his Week 5 game against Jacksonville. Pelissero initially reported that Hurts was expected to miss “ multiple months after new imaging ” revealed several blood clots in his lungs. He also claimed doctors had advised Hurts “not to sleep” following an initial diagnosis in London. “ How committed is Jalen Hurts to football? ” Pelissero wrote on X. He added that Hurts had been awake for roughly 36 hours when he started against the Jaguars, saying, “he had been awake for roughly 36 hours… throwing for 220 yards and a TD.” MORE: Fans react to Michael Robinson’s apology to Jalen Hurts However, Pelissero later updated his account after speaking with Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn. “Just spoke to Jalen Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, who clarified that while Hurts was up until early Sunday morning getting evaluated at a hospital, he was able to sleep upon rejoining the team and the Eagles set aside a room for him at the stadium,” Pelissero wrote. “Videos from the stadium show Hurts coming onto the field just before kickoff and he felt rested enough to play.” Just spoke to Jalen Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, who clarified that while Hurts was up until early Sunday morning getting evaluated at a hospital, he was able to sleep upon rejoining the team and the Eagles set aside a room for him at the stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The clarification changes an important detail surrounding Hurts’ preparation for the Jacksonville game. Rather than remaining awake for roughly 36 hours, he was able to rest after his hospital evaluation. Still, the larger medical concern remains serious. Subsequent testing reportedly revealed blood clots in Hurts’ lungs, prompting expectations that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season. The Eagles quarterback had played against Jacksonville despite the earlier diagnosis, completing 18 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown. His availability became a major talking point after the subsequent medical findings. MORE: Former Eagles receiver sends prayers to Jalen Hurts after health scare Hurts’ situation has also led to debate about the importance of accurate reporting when discussing potentially serious health conditions. Pelissero’s correction provides additional context without changing the reported severity of the diagnosis. Videos from the stadium show Hurts… https://t.co/G35Tn1poa4 — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) October 19, 2026 Jalen Hurts’ health concerns overshadow his commitment Tottenham, ENG; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The clarification changes an important detail surrounding Hurts’ preparation for the Jacksonville game. Rather than remaining awake for roughly 36 hours, he was able to rest after his hospital evaluation. Still, the larger medical concern remains serious. Subsequent testing reportedly revealed blood clots in Hurts’ lungs, prompting expectations that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season. The Eagles quarterback had played against Jacksonville despite the earlier diagnosis, completing 18 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown. His availability became a major talking point after the subsequent medical findings. MORE: Former Eagles receiver sends prayers to Jalen Hurts after health scare Hurts’ situation has also led to debate about the importance of accurate reporting when discussing potentially serious health conditions. Pelissero’s correction provides additional context without changing the reported severity of the diagnosis. Meanwhile, the Eagles’ statement says, “ We expect a full recovery … anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners.” Philadelphia must now prepare to move forward without its franchise quarterback. Hurts’ recovery will take priority as the Eagles navigate the remainder of their season. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Former NFL player makes Peyton Manning request after Colts fire GM Chris Ballard
item.description: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are making a drastic change, with Chris Ballard being shown the door. One former NFL star has brought franchise legend Peyton Manning into it. The Indianapolis Colts suffered a defeat at the hands of the winless Tennessee Titans. Not only was it bad enough that the team lost against such a poorly performing franchise, the fact that Tennessee are division rivals made it much worse. It was the final chapter in the story of Chris Ballard’s Colts tenure. Ballard spent nearly 10 years as Indianapolis Colts GM, and during most of that time, the team was nothing more than average. They lost more games than they won over the course of his career. Trading for Sauce Gardner and giving Daniel Jones a big extension had him on the hot seat, and the Titans loss sealed his fate. People are already talking about what is next for the Colts. Robert Griffin III calls for Peyton Manning to return to the Indianapolis Colts Peyton Manning has been a name discussed as a potential GM for the Colts for many years. The quarterback led the Colts to the Super Bowl during his 13 years with the franchise. He is a team legend and one of the NFL’s most respected personalities. Reports suggest that he is strongly being considered for Ballard’s job, and now Robert Griffin III has openly called for the team to make the hire. “The Indianapolis Colts should hire Peyton Manning as their new GM,” RGIII said without getting too much into the details. Many fans seemed to agree with him too, it seems that Manning would be quite a popular choice among Colts’ supporters. However things shake out, it really was time for the Colts to move on from Ballard. If they actually manage to land Peyton, that might go a long way in softening the blow of recent failures they’ve had to witness. Smith boldly reveals what John Harbaugh should tell Cam Skattebo ‘All he cares about’ – 49ers’ John Lynch reveals ‘the great thing’ about Brock Purdy

item.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Sends Message on Defense vs. Commanders
item.description: Kyle Shanahan talked about the defense making the plays needed on Monday. Getty The Washington Commanders threatened to spoil the San Francisco 49ers‘ night, but the Niners defense rose to the occasion right on time. Defensive ends Romello Height and Keion White tag-teaming on Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels ended the game with an explanation point for the 49ers (6-0) in a 23-17 win. Washington rallied from 20-3 down to have a shot at winning the game in the final seconds. “I was really proud of the defense just being able to overcome… all those penalties and us [the offense] not being able to help them out there at the end,” 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Monday. “I love how our defense hits.” Osa Odighizuwa, Mykel Williams, and Gracen Halton also sacked Daniels in the win. The 49ers had 11 tackles for loss as a team, and Jaden Dugger led the defense with a team-high 11 tackles. The 49ers gave up two touchdown drives in the second half, but the Niners defense kept the Commanders off the board for the final two drives of the game to preserve the win. To Shanahan’s point, the 49ers offense went cold in the second half with three punts and a field goal. San Francisco will now have a short week to work out those kinks before a road game against the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 25. Brock Purdy Gives Shout Out to Defense Niners quarterback Brock Purdy can’t deny that the defense bailed out the offense in the second half. Purdy led an 11-play, 65-yard drive in the third quarter, which resulted in a field goal, so things looked on par with the 20-point first half initially. Then, the 49ers managed negative yardage on six plays in the fourth quarter, as the Commanders threatened. “Obviously, offensively and for myself in the second half…it’s tough,” Purdy told reporters on Monday. “For our defense to do what they did at the end, that was really impressive.” Washington made it 23-17 on Daniels’ touchdown pass to running back Rachaad White with 9:22 left in the fourth quarter and things looked like a far cry from the 49ers’ first half cushion of 20-3. The 49ers offense hardly gave the defense a break after the Commanders’ 10-play, 80-yard scoring drive because the ensuing 49ers possession lasted 1:36. San Francisco gave up 61 yards on 13 plays on the next Commanders’ possession, but the secondary rose to the occasion especially. Malik Mustapha broke things up in the end zone for the 49ers, which thwarted a potential touchdown pass to Treylon Burks on fourth down. 49ers Keep Winning Despite Injuries While many of the 49ers injuries on offense, the defense has significant players missing, too. That includes defensive lineman Nick Bosa, and the 49ers defense didn’t have linebacker Dre Greenlaw due to a suspension. Greenlaw had 18 tackles and a sack this season, and Bosa had three tackles in his two games played. As for the offense, it looks like a MASH united. The 49ers survived without wide receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robi

item.title: Max Verstappen defends British teammate after social media abuse: ‘I need to speak out’
item.description: Max Verstappen has hit out at “personal attacks” directed at teammate Chris Lulham on social media while competing at an endurance event in Portugal over the weekend. The four-time F1 world champion was racing in the GT World Challenge on Saturday for his own independent team, Verstappen Racing, and was joined by British drivers Lulham and Ben Barnicoat. In the middle phase of the endurance race on Saturday, Lulham received a drive-through penalty which pushed his team down to 24th when the Dutchman took over. Verstappen recovered to finish ninth, in a finale which included a dramatic late overtake on Charles Leclerc’s brother, Arthur. VERSTAPPEN VS LECLERC 🔥 Max Verstappen did battle with Arthur Leclerc during an incredible recovery drive in the GT World Challenge that saw the Dutchman finish P9 following a drive-through penalty. pic.twitter.com/9ZZhkQyUxS — Sky Sports F1 (@SkySportsF1) October 18, 2026 Yet in the aftermath, Lulham was subject to abuse online and Verstappen – just a few days after Franco Colapinto implored his fans to stop abusing fellow F1 drivers – released a short statement on Instagram condemning those responsible. "I also feel I need to speak up about the hate and harassment Chris has received after the race,” he said. “Everyone can have their opinions about what happened on track, but these personal attacks are not okay. "Chris had a really strong stint, and mistakes can happen. There’s no place for this kind of abuse in our sport or anywhere else." Verstappen’s message comes a few days after Alpine F1 driver Colapinto told his fanbase “you’re not helping me” after a number of incidents involving social media abuse of fellow drivers on the grid. Verstappen was racing in between two F1 triple-headers, the second of which starts with the United States Grand Prix in Austin this weekend. The Red Bull driver has won the last two races, in Malaysia and Singapore, and is currently fourth in the drivers’ standings.

item.title: How the Seattle Pilots became the Milwaukee Brewers ... in six days
item.description: How long have the Milwaukee Brewers been around in their current, major-league form? That seems like a simple question, but as graphics shown during broadcasts of the National League Championship Series reminded us, there are two ways to look at it. The franchise has been around since 1969, but the Brewers since 1970 after an abrupt move from Seattle. Since-retired Milwaukee Journal Sentinel sportswriter Tom Haudricourt wrote about the topic extensively in 2020 for a book on the team’s 50th anniversary. Here’s a synopsis of the Braves-to-Pilots-to-Brewers history of Major League Baseball in Milwaukee. When did the Milwaukee Brewers become a major-league team? On April 1, 1970, U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Sidney Volinn gave final approval in Seattle for the sale of the struggling expansion franchise, the Seattle Pilots , to Milwaukee Brewers Inc., a group led by Bud Selig. BUY BREWERS BOOK: Celebrate Brewers' pennant with book, page print from Journal Sentinel When and why did the Braves leave Milwaukee? The Braves came to Milwaukee from Boston in 1953, at which time the team’s minor-league affiliate Class AAA Milwaukee Brewers were moved to Toledo. The Braves won the World Series in 1957 , but an ownership change in ’62 set the stage for their departure after the 1965 season as Chicago-based William Bartholomay sought a better business climate and was promised a new stadium. A criminal complaint was filed in Milwaukee County Circuit Court to try to stop the move , alleging antitrust violations, and an initial ruling required the National League to place a new team in Milwaukee in 1967, but that was later overturned. Who were other key players in bringing baseball back to Milwaukee? Selig’s group included local businessmen Edmund Fitzgerald (Northwestern Mutual Life), Ben Barkin (Barkin, Herman, Solochek and Paulsen public relations), Robert Uihlein Jr. (Schlitz Brewing) and Irwin Maier (The Journal Company). Bud Selig lobbied for National League expansion teams The National League awarded two expansion franchises in 1968. When NL President Warren Giles announced the additions at a May 1968 owners’ meeting, Selig saw an “M” forming in Giles’ mouth and thought Milwaukee was getting a team. Instead it was Montreal that would be added, giving MLB its first Canadian team, along with San Diego. At the same time, the American League added the Kansas City Royals, a replacement in the city after the A’s moved to Oakland, and the Seattle Pilots. Bud Selig tried to move the Chicago White Sox Among Selig’s ideas to bring MLB back to Milwaukee was a deal to buy the Chicago White Sox from co-owner Art Allyn, but the American League vetoed that sale. Allyn instead sold his half of the team to his brother, co-owner John, in 1969. Who were the Seattle Pilots? The Seattle Pilots, one of two American League expansion teams and four in MLB that season, joined Major League Baseball in 1969. item.content:encoded: How long have the Milwaukee Brewers been around in their current, major-league form? That seems like a simple question, but as graphics shown during broadcasts of the National League Championship Series reminded us, there are two ways to look at it. The franchise has been around since 1969, but the Brewers since 1970 after an abrupt move from Seattle. Since-retired Milwaukee Journal Sentinel sportswriter Tom Haudricourt wrote about the topic extensively in 2020 for a book on the team’s 50th anniversary. Here’s a synopsis of the Braves-to-Pilots-to-Brewers history of Major League Baseball in Milwaukee. When did the Milwaukee Brewers become a major-league team? On April 1, 1970, U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Sidney Volinn gave final approval in Seattle for the sale of the struggling expansion franchise, the Seattle Pilots , to Milwaukee Brewers Inc., a group led by Bud Selig. BUY BREWERS BOOK: Celebrate Brewers' pennant with book, page print from Journal Sentinel When and why did the Braves leave Milwaukee? The Braves came to Milwaukee from Boston in 1953, at which time the team’s minor-league affiliate Class AAA Milwaukee Brewers were moved to Toledo. The Braves won the World Series in 1957 , but an ownership change in ’62 set the stage for their departure after the 1965 season as Chicago-based William Bartholomay sought a better business climate and was promised a new stadium. A criminal complaint was filed in Milwaukee County Circuit Court to try to stop the move , alleging antitrust violations, and an initial ruling required the National League to place a new team in Milwaukee in 1967, but that was later overturned. Who were other key players in bringing baseball back to Milwaukee? Selig’s group included local businessmen Edmund Fitzgerald (Northwestern Mutual Life), Ben Barkin (Barkin, Herman, Solochek and Paulsen public relations), Robert Uihlein Jr. (Schlitz Brewing) and Irwin Maier (The Journal Company). Bud Selig lobbied for National League expansion teams The National League awarded two expansion franchises in 1968. When NL President Warren Giles announced the additions at a May 1968 owners’ meeting, Selig saw an “M” forming in Giles’ mouth and thought Milwaukee was getting a team. Instead it was Montreal that would be added, giving MLB its first Canadian team, along with San Diego. At the same time, the American League added the Kansas City Royals, a replacement in the city after the A’s moved to Oakland, and the Seattle Pilots. Bud Selig tried to move the Chicago White Sox Among Selig’s ideas to bring MLB back to Milwaukee was a deal to buy the Chicago White Sox from co-owner Art Allyn, but the American League vetoed that sale. Allyn instead sold his half of the team to his brother, co-owner John, in 1969. Who were the Seattle Pilots? The Seattle Pilots, one of two American League expansion teams and four in MLB that season, joined Major League Baseball in 1969. The original plan was to have until 1971 to prepare, but Kansas City’s launch was pushed up and the AL required both to join at the same time. The city had been home to the Seattle Rainiers of the Class AAA Pacific Coast League. Former Rainiers pitcher and general manager and PCL president Dewey Soriano led the group behind the Pilots, Pacific Northwest Sports Inc. How did the Pilots become the Brewers? The Pilots struggled on the field (64–98) and at the turnstile (678,000 fans), and Pacific Northwest Sports was underfunded. Soriano asked William R. Daley, owner of the Cleveland franchise, to take on much of the purchase price in exchange for which he became the largest shareholder. PNSI filed for bankruptcy, and on April 1, 1970, the sale of the team to Milwaukee Brewers Inc. for $10.8 million was given final approval. The Pilots became the Brewers in just six days Spring training was coming to an end as the courtroom drama played out, and as the team broke camp in Tempe, Arizona, the driver of the equipment truck stopped in Las Vegas to await directions on which direction to head. The season opener was set for April 7 at County Stadium. With no time to order new uniforms, the Pilots’ name and logo were removed from each jersey and “Brewers” was stitched over that space and an “M” replaced the “S” on the caps. The team arrived late April 5 to an impromptu pep rally at Mitchell Field and two days later lost their opener 12-0 to the California Angels at County Stadium in front of 37,237. item.title: 3 Biggest Storylines to Watch on NBA Opening Night
item.description: Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) and guard Jaylen Brown (7) and Boston Celtics guard Hugo Gonzalez (28) go for a loose ball during the third quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor NBA opening night storylines rarely offer this much intrigue across a single slate. The 2026–27 season tips off Tuesday, October 20, with three games on NBC and Peacock: Boston Celtics at Detroit Pistons at 3 p.m. ET, Philadelphia 76ers at Knicks at 7 p.m., and Oklahoma Thunder at San Antonio Spurs at 9:30 p.m. ET. From a championship celebration to a blockbuster debut and a Western Conference Finals rematch, each game comes with a question that could shape the season ahead. 1. Can the Pistons Take the Next Step? Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) drives against Boston Celtics guard Derrick White (9) in the second half at Little Caesars Arena. Photo Credit: Rick Osentoski, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Detroit finished 60–22 last season to claim the Eastern Conference’s top seed, but its postseason run fell short of expectations. The Pistons struggled in both the first and second rounds, exposing weaknesses that their regular-season record had masked. As the Pistons open the new campaign against Boston, Detroit will look to build on last season’s success while addressing the issues that prevented them from advancing further in the playoffs. Cade Cunningham remains the centerpiece, but the Pistons supporting cast will be worth watching. The departures of Tobias Harris and Isaiah Stewart leave questions about the team’s depth and frontcourt rotation, while additions such as John Collins and Isaiah Joe offer different ways to address those needs. Boston will provide a serious test. Detroit must show that its supporting cas t can contribute consistently on offense and that its offseason moves have strengthened the roster. While one game won’t determine the Pistons’ ceiling, it could offer an early indication of how well the team has addressed the weaknesses that contributed to its playoff struggles last season. 2. Can the 76ers’ New Stars Deliver Against the Champions? Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) reacts in a game against the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Photo Credit: Bill Streicher, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The New York Knicks will raise their championship banner before hosting Philadelphia, celebrating their first NBA title since 1973. The occasion alone makes this one of the night’s biggest attractions, but the 76ers’ revamped roster adds another layer of intrigue. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown will make their 76ers debuts alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey . On paper, that combination gives the 76ers an imposing collection of talent. The challenge is turning individual ability into a cohesive team. With several players accustomed to carrying substantial offensive responsibilities, questions about ball distribution, late-game decision-making and defensive chemi
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) and guard Jaylen Brown (7) and Boston Celtics guard Hugo Gonzalez (28) go for a loose ball during the third quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor NBA opening night storylines rarely offer this much intrigue across a single slate. The 2026–27 season tips off Tuesday, October 20, with three games on NBC and Peacock: Boston Celtics at Detroit Pistons at 3 p.m. ET, Philadelphia 76ers at Knicks at 7 p.m., and Oklahoma Thunder at San Antonio Spurs at 9:30 p.m. ET. From a championship celebration to a blockbuster debut and a Western Conference Finals rematch, each game comes with a question that could shape the season ahead. 1. Can the Pistons Take the Next Step? Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) drives against Boston Celtics guard Derrick White (9) in the second half at Little Caesars Arena. Photo Credit: Rick Osentoski, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Detroit finished 60–22 last season to claim the Eastern Conference’s top seed, but its postseason run fell short of expectations. The Pistons struggled in both the first and second rounds, exposing weaknesses that their regular-season record had masked. As the Pistons open the new campaign against Boston, Detroit will look to build on last season’s success while addressing the issues that prevented them from advancing further in the playoffs. Cade Cunningham remains the centerpiece, but the Pistons supporting cast will be worth watching. The departures of Tobias Harris and Isaiah Stewart leave questions about the team’s depth and frontcourt rotation, while additions such as John Collins and Isaiah Joe offer different ways to address those needs. Boston will provide a serious test. Detroit must show that its supporting cas t can contribute consistently on offense and that its offseason moves have strengthened the roster. While one game won’t determine the Pistons’ ceiling, it could offer an early indication of how well the team has addressed the weaknesses that contributed to its playoff struggles last season. 2. Can the 76ers’ New Stars Deliver Against the Champions? Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) reacts in a game against the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Photo Credit: Bill Streicher, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The New York Knicks will raise their championship banner before hosting Philadelphia, celebrating their first NBA title since 1973. The occasion alone makes this one of the night’s biggest attractions, but the 76ers’ revamped roster adds another layer of intrigue. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown will make their 76ers debuts alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey . On paper, that combination gives the 76ers an imposing collection of talent. The challenge is turning individual ability into a cohesive team. With several players accustomed to carrying substantial offensive responsibilities, questions about ball distribution, late-game decision-making and defensive chemistry will follow Philadelphia into the opener. Embiid and Maxey already have established roles, so integrating James and Brown without disrupting that foundation will be crucial. The Knicks offer an immediate measuring stick. Their championship core returns with the confidence and continuity that come from winning it all, while Philadelphia must prove its offseason additions can translate into results. If the 76ers can compete with the defending champions from the opening tip, a strong showing would offer an early glimpse of their potential. 3. Thunder-Spurs Renews the West’s Biggest Rivalry Oklahoma City Thunder center Chet Holmgren (7) drives against San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) in the fourth quarter during game seven of the Western Conference Finals for the 2026 NBA playoffs at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The opening-night tripleheader concludes with a rematch of the 2026 Western Conference Finals, where San Antonio defeated Oklahoma City in seven games before losing to New York in the NBA Finals. This matchup carries more significance than a typical season opener. The Thunder and Spurs met 12 times last season across the regular season, the NBA Cup semifinals and the playoffs, establishing a rivalry that should continue to define the Western Conference. Oklahoma City faces the challenge of replacing several valuable rotation pieces who contributed in different ways, from perimeter defense and three-point shooting to efficient play on both ends of the floor. Maintaining that depth and versatility while finding new solutions against San Antonio will be an early challenge. For the Spurs, Victor Wembanyama and company have an opportunity to build on a Finals run that exceeded many expectations. Neither team needs to prove its entire season’s worth in one game. Still, with both expected to contend in the West, this rematch offers an early look at how they have evolved since their last postseason meeting. The Last Word Opening night offers an early look at three teams facing very different expectations. Detroit wants to prove its breakthrough can lead to a deeper playoff run, Philadelphia must show its star-studded roster can function as a team, and Oklahoma City will get an immediate opportunity to measure itself against the opponent that ended its season. Which of these three opening-night games are you most interested in watching? Drop your takes in the comments! item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Villarreal’s Iñigo Pérez ready to meet Iraola again in test of old bond
item.description: Refused a work permit at Bournemouth, Pérez comes face to face with Liverpool’s head coach in Champions League On Iñigo Pérez’s first day as a head coach he took a call from Andoni Iraola, just as he had every day for months. They had known each other for 22 years, lived in the same residency, come through the same academy and played in the same team; they had worked side by side, manager and assistant, and embarked on an adventure together. Now, though, Pérez was having to go it alone. At 36, he had become what his friend thought he would be from the moment they met, just not so soon. “He wished me luck and said he was there for me,” Pérez said, “said that if I ever needed anything …” Well, maybe not anything . Continue reading...

The federation’s disciplinary council said it had upheld the charge against ⁠the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of €255 (£215). Ronaldo left Portugal’s base in ⁠Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark this month, having accused ‌Jesus of twice ‌breaking his word about his role after he was an ‌unused substitute against Norway. item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...
